Each had loaded **2 million barrels of Saudi crude** at **Juaymah**; both had been sailing dark; **all crew safe**; **no claim of responsibility**, with Marisks, Kpler, UKMTO and Bloomberg all describing the projectiles as *“unknown.”* The attribution is **logged as an open question**, not assumed. **Trump** called the strikes *“large and powerful”* and warned that if Iran retaliates *“they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level — but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings”*; to Fox News he described the targeting himself: *“They tried to rebuild their radar because they can't see anything. > **Daily update — September 1, 2026 (Day 187; August 31 data cycle).** **Iran answered Larak by name and by operation, and the United States answered the answer with a threat rather than a strike.** Overnight into **Monday August 31** the **IRGC Aerospace Force** ran a combined missile-and-drone operation it named **"Punishment of the Aggressor"** against **King Hussein** and **Al Azraq** air bases in **Jordan**; Iran's Foreign Ministry said the bases *"had been used to launch and support attacks on Iran."* Iran's **army** separately said **dozens of drones** were launched at US forces and helicopters at **Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates**. It is the **first two-country Iranian retaliation of this phase** and the **first named Iranian operation since the pause**. **The damage claims and the denials do not meet, and all three accounts are logged.** The IRGC claims *"heavy damage"* to technical infrastructure, maintenance facilities and fighter-jet positions at both Jordanian bases. **Jordan's military** says it **intercepted eight ballistic missiles** before they threatened infrastructure or troops, with **no injuries** — while **two Jordanian security sources** said some missiles were **not** successfully intercepted. The **UAE Ministry of Defence** called reports that missiles struck Al Menhad **"false,"** urged reliance on official sources rather than rumours, and confirmed only that its air force **intercepted one drone** over territorial waters approaching from Iran. **No casualties were reported by any party, and the United States — which alone knows what happened to its own aircraft — said nothing about any of the three bases.** Logged as `punishment-of-the-aggressor-damage-claims-august-2026`. **The American answer was verbal.** President Trump told Fox News the United States would **"hit them hard"** and **"hit them very hard"** — while in the same remarks describing the Strait as being in **"extremely good shape,"** Iran's economy, military and leadership as **"largely deteriorated,"** and adding **"it doesn't mean we won't smack them to see what happens."** **No second confirmed US strike inside Iran followed in the next twenty-four hours.** **CENTCOM put the enforcement frame on the record in its own name**, rejecting the IRGC's *"act of aggression"* characterisation as **"absolutely false"** and stating that *"US forces took **limited, precise action** against IRGC **minelaying forces** posing an **imminent threat** in the Strait of Hormuz."* **The cycle's hardest data are two documents, and one of them corrects this reference.** *First:* on **August 30-31** the Army extended the Middle East deployment of the **82nd Airborne Division** to a **full twelve months**, into 2027 — and the published unit list is a **Division Headquarters, the 1st Brigade Combat Team, the Combat Aviation Brigade, DIVARTY, the 307th Division Engineer Battalion, 3-4 Air Defense Artillery** and a sustainment element, **approximately 2,000 soldiers** deployed in March. This document has carried *"approximately 1,000 paratroopers"* and the statement that **no brigade combat team, division headquarters or corps-level enabler set had been identified in theatre at any point in the war**. Both were wrong and are corrected here; the units arrived in March, and the extension letter is what made their composition public. The extension **adds no soldiers, moves nobody forward and assigns no mission** — it holds a force in place because there is nothing to relieve it with. *Second:* **The Washington Post published the August 14 edition of the Secretary of Defense Orders Book.** **Four formal non-concurs** were filed against continued allocation to the Iran theatre — **Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle**, **INDOPACOM's Adm. Samuel Paparo**, **EUCOM's Gen. Alexus Grynkewich** and **SOUTHCOM** — with the Army and Air Force chiefs concurring while recording increased risk. Caudle: the Navy **"cannot sustain its current level of support"** absent an end date, with **barely a quarter of the destroyer fleet ready to deploy**. **More than half** the cruise-missile and advanced air-defence inventories expended; **~25% of the Reaper fleet** lost; **THAAD redeployed from South Korea**; the **USS George Washington** moved from Japan to the Gulf, **leaving the Pacific without carrier coverage**. The collective formulation as reported: **"We will carry out the orders, but at a price."** Pentagon spokesman **Sean Parnell** called the leak **"a crime"** and **"a betrayal of the force"** while confirming that the Secretary sees non-concurs *"constantly."* **The Larak toll resolved to three IRGC personnel killed and two injured**, two named as **Hamid Avazzadeh** and **Ali Fayazi**. **Kpler put Kharg loadings at 135,000 bpd in August against 1.98m bpd in February** — a **93% collapse achieved by blockade, with nobody on the island**. **UKMTO published the first full transit count in weeks: 101 outbound and 103 inbound in the seven days to August 28**, traffic *"significantly reduced"* and **~90% below** pre-conflict, with **16 of 18 projectile-strike incidents since July 6 on the southern Omani route**. **Brent closed above $90 for the first time since the pause began** at **$90.78**, +26.1% on the pre-crisis baseline. > **Daily update — August 31, 2026 (Day 186; August 30 data cycle).** **The twenty-nine-night strike pause broke, and it broke at Larak Island — the piece of ground through which Iran administers the traffic it claimed the day before to be permitting.** On **Sunday August 30** US forces struck **two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island**. A US official said the IRGC *"was preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the strait when US forces struck"*; *Axios* reported the rockets were armed with sea mines. It is the **first confirmed US strike inside Iran since August 1** — the longest pause of the war. **The target set is the finding, not the fact of the strike.** Five days earlier the President declared every mine cleared from the Strait's international waters under a **"Zero Tolerance"** rule — *"Any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed"* — and two days earlier CENTCOM commander **Admiral Brad Cooper** declared the lanes free of Iranian sea mines and called it a *"major milestone."* A resumption of mining from Larak would have falsified both claims inside a week. The United States **destroyed the launchers and left the island**. Whether that is a declared rule enforced on its own terms or the first night of a renewed campaign **cannot be settled from August 30** and is logged as open question `larak-strike-enforcement-or-campaign-resumption-august-2026`. **The IRGC vowed retribution and Iran struck back with missiles, not men.** The IRGC said the attack caused *"the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots"* without a toll, told IRIB *"we will take retribution,"* and through spokesman **Sardar Mohebi** called the strike *"a strategic and fatal mistake"* with consequences *"in both the economic and military arenas"*; parliament's **Ebrahim Azizi**: *"Retaliation is coming."* Iranian missiles were fired at **US forces in Jordan**; a US source said *"nearly all incoming missiles have been intercepted at this point"* with *"no significant impacts so far."* **The cycle's structural finding is a symmetry new to this record: both commands now claim permissioning authority over the same water.** Cooper, August 28: *"No ships have entered or left an Iranian port without our permission, and we have only allowed ships to pass through on humanitarian grounds."* Gharibabadi, August 29: *"Any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran."* The two address adjacent but distinguishable water and are **not strictly incompatible**; **neither is verifiable from open sources**. **A third claim is contradicted by the only disinterested measurement in the set:** CENTCOM says Iranian oil exports have been **zero** since mid-July and Iran's own **central bank governor** said the same on August 20, while **Kpler** records approximately **260,000 barrels a day loaded** at Iranian ports in August — down **more than 80%** on August 2025 and **~70%** on July, but not zero. Logged as `iran-oil-exports-zero-or-loading-august-2026`. **The Supreme Leader wrote to the Gulf, and Reuters supplied the reason for his absence.** In an Islamic Unity Week message **Mojtaba Khamenei** told *"the rulers of Islamic countries, especially the countries of West Asia and the Gulf"* to *"identify your real enemy, understand his plan and confront it,"* calling for **mutual defence** — his **second written statement in two days** — and Reuters reported for the first time that he has not been seen in public **because he was injured in the February 28 strikes** that killed his father. **The financial track reached its loudest and landed softest.** **Bessent** told the AP another bank would be designated this week — *"This is going to be financial violence if we have to"* — said *"all options are on the table"* on China ahead of the **G20 in Asheville, North Carolina**, and called reports of his reluctance *"a completely false narrative that the media picked up on."* *Fortune* reported the world **"mostly shrugged off"** the threat: **no Chinese institution designated for a third consecutive package**, Iranian bank branches still open in **Dubai**, flights still running to **Turkey**, **Pakistan** saying it *"is not obliged"* to follow unilateral sanctions, and former Treasury official **Alex Zerden** saying the actions *"do not match the hype."* **Russia announced its own escalation in advance:** the Defence Ministry said its forces *"have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure"* in retaliation for Ukraine's refinery campaign — logged as a stated intention, not an executed act (`russia-announced-energy-campaign-order-or-signal-august-2026`). The **Myla** toll rose to **38 killed, 20 injured, 4 missing**; Ukraine struck the **Kirishi refinery**, Russia's second-largest; Zelensky put the week at **~2,000 drones, 1,600+ bombs and 31 missiles, including North Korean ballistic missiles**. **Markets:** Brent **$89.75**, **+1.87%** on the strike, **+24.7%** on the ~$72 baseline; CENTCOM's blockade tally **83 redirected / 3 disabled**; SPR below **300m bbl**; pump price **$4.12**. **Ground rung unchanged — and this is the cycle that tested it.** The United States had a ground-suitable objective on a small island inside the Strait, with **2,200-2,500 Marines of the 11th MEU embarked and untasked a day's steaming away**, and it used aircraft. **No landing, no lodgement, no Kharg action, no draft order** — every execution indicator at zero for a **185th consecutive day**.

> **Daily update — August 30, 2026 (Day 185; August 29 data cycle).** **The day after the President said no American troops had deployed into Iran, Iran's deputy foreign minister said the Strait is still closed — and that every ship crossing it does so "in coordination with Iran."** On **August 29** Deputy Foreign Minister **Kazem Gharibabadi** said: *"The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran."* **That is new in kind.** For six months the public dispute has been binary — Washington says open, Tehran says closed. Tehran has now advanced a third position that is consistent with **both** governments' published numbers: that the traffic the United States cites as proof of openness is traffic Iran is **permitting**. No permissioning or clearance record exists in the open source base on either side, and none of the named operators has said whether Iranian clearance was sought; the claim is logged as contested and unresolved. **The Iran-Oman understanding is confirmed as reached and simultaneously suspended,** its implementation conditioned on the United States honouring the **Islamabad memorandum** — and on Gharibabadi's own description it would **close both** the temporary **northern route near Larak Island** and the **UN-authorised southern route** hugging Oman's coast, replacing them with a **single seven-mile corridor** whose entry and part of whose exit lie in **Iranian territorial waters**. The southern route is the channel announced under the June MOU, which Iran said violated that agreement and against whose users it attacked shipping. That is not a restoration of the pre-war regime; it is a different regime. The **IRGC Navy** called American statements that the Strait is open *"an obvious lie"* and its own control *"completely decisive."* **The transit data ran the other way and is logged against the rhetoric.** *USNI News*, citing **Lloyd's List Intelligence**, recorded **114 transits between August 17 and August 27** — up **more than 30%** on the week, led by tankers and gas carriers — with **at least 42 westbound** transits against **29** the week prior, among them crude tankers from **Sinokor** and **ADNOC** and Saudi- and Kuwaiti-owned hulls, against a pre-war baseline near **138 vessels a day**. **Goldman Sachs** puts Persian Gulf exports at **15-16 million bpd** against a pre-conflict **22-24 million** and a **March low near 5-6 million**. **The six-month economic admission came from the top of the Iranian state, and it came in writing.** Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** — who *Al Jazeera* recorded has **not appeared publicly since his father's death on February 28** — issued a **Government Week** message calling for serious attention to *"inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services,"* stating that *"the main key to resolving all these issues lies in relying increasingly on domestic production,"* and setting out a roadmap to **gradually phase the US dollar out** of the economy with **"resistance economy"** policies at the centre of government. **Pezeshkian** put numbers to it: exports and imports **down nearly 35%**, roughly **90 million barrels** of oil sold during the June MOU window, against **66% annual inflation** — while saying Iran will *"stand strong against any aggressor"* and will *"not bow to any threat."* Tehran formalised its posture as **"diplomacy and defence,"** *"complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings"*: Ambassador to Germany **Majid Nili** said the path of dialogue *"is still being pursued"*; **Araghchi** posted *"Pressure doesn't work"*; Acting Defence Minister Brig. Gen. **Majid Ebn al-Reza** said adversaries *"will become aware of Iran's surprises in due time"*; Army Commander **Amir Hatami** said the drone and missile stockpile had been fired *"with the utmost intensity until the last moment."* **The American offensive's geography was named and Beijing is not on it.** *Iran International*'s analysis of the Banque Misr action found the campaign aimed at **Dubai, Istanbul and Baghdad** as Iran's financial channels rather than at Beijing — the second consecutive package to spare China's major banks, now with an articulated geography rather than merely an absence. **Banque Misr UAE** said it affirms *"full respect for the relevant regulatory and legal frameworks"* and treats the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking *"with the utmost seriousness and attention."* **The domestic constraint acquired a date, for the first time in the record.** Reuters and Bloomberg reported the President will meet **at least ten fuel makers and distributors** — **Valero**, **Marathon Petroleum** and **PBF Energy** expected — on **Tuesday September 1**, over gasoline **above $4 a gallon** and diesel **near $6**, the highest seasonal level ever recorded and roughly **a dollar above the February 28 level**, ahead of November's midterms. A White House official would not confirm, saying only the administration *"will make a decision that is best for consumers, farmers, and energy supply chains."* **On the ground rung, the load-bearing movement was a dispersal.** CENTCOM published its first imagery of Marine ground personnel in this theatre in some weeks — and it shows **Marines refuelling an MV-22 Osprey**, published rather than concealed, which is the inverse of pre-assault operational security. Meanwhile the **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group has split**: **USS Boxer** remains in the **Arabian Sea** while **USS Comstock** — the dock landing ship that would put vehicles and heavy equipment ashore — is now in the **Indian Ocean**. **USS Tripoli** is in homeport at **Sasebo, Japan**, having offloaded the 31st MEU at Okinawa on July 22. Troop strength in CENTCOM remains **~50,000**, reaffirmed by the Pentagon on August 28, none inside Iran. **Kharg Island was not seized, not targeted and not mentioned.** **In Ukraine, the deadliest single attack of the year — and a causal dispute both sides' own accounts make unresolvable.** At about **20:10 local on August 28** a Russian drone struck an enterprise in **Myla**, five kilometres west of Kyiv, touching off a fire and sustained **ammunition detonations** that killed **at least 37 people**, among them the mayor of Dmytrivka, damaging a **care home for elderly and disabled people** and forcing **380+** evacuations. Ukrainian prosecutors said the site held *"explosive objects"* and **Zelensky** pointed to ammunition; **Russia's Defence Ministry** said it struck a warehouse storing **components and launch boosters for long-range drones**. Both accounts agree munitions were present and that secondary detonation drove the toll; they disagree on everything that determines responsibility, and the site has been destroyed. Ukraine downed or suppressed **233 drones** overnight into August 29 as national air alerts ran into a **third consecutive day**. **A twenty-ninth consecutive night passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran.** The war remains **air, naval, financial and judicial** — **no landing, no Kharg seizure, no draft order**. > **Daily update — August 29, 2026 (Day 184).** **Six months, and the President described his own war as one "in which no American troops have deployed into Iran."** The US-Israeli war on Iran reached its **six-month mark on August 28**, against a presidential forecast on **February 29** that the fight could last **four to five weeks**; reporting across outlets converged on the finding that **none of the six objectives** Trump outlined at the launch has been fully achieved. Defending the campaign, Trump characterised it as one **"in which no American troops have deployed into Iran"** — the **first affirmative statement by the commander-in-chief** of the precise negative this audit has tracked for 184 consecutive days by inference from fleet trackers, force-disposition reporting and the silence of an Iranian government that would announce a landing within hours. It is a description of the past six months, not a commitment about the next six, and it is recorded as such. **The American instrument of the cycle was financial and for the first time it cut a bank out of the dollar.** Treasury, acting through **FinCEN**, proposed a rule severing the **six United Arab Emirates branches of Egypt's Banque Misr** from correspondent banking with US financial institutions, over approximately **$1.8 billion** processed for roughly **103 companies** potentially forming part of Iran's shadow banking network between **January 2024 and June 2026**. **Scott Bessent**: *"Banque Misr UAE decided to find out the hard way, and today, we are taking the first step in holding it accountable for its continued, egregious support of the Iranian regime."* The limits are recorded with the action: it is a **proposed rule with a 30-day comment period**, not a designation; **Cairo and the Paris, Frankfurt, Riyadh, Beirut and Djibouti branches** continue to transact in dollars; **China's major banks were spared for a second consecutive package**, reportedly out of reluctance to penalise major trading partners including China and India. Treasury also targeted **Bank Melli's UAE branch manager** and a **Hong Kong entity**. **Tehran moved toward paper rather than water.** **Mohsen Rezaei** said Iran is drawing up a **list of conditions** for reopening the Strait at the mediators' request — *"The US must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran's conditions, and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz"* — confirming agreed **Iran-Oman corridor coordinates** partly in Omani and partly in Iranian waters, with a **central channel** available if Washington complies. The price is unchanged across four mediators in five days: **end the blockade, compensation, sanctions relief, end the war**. The **IRGC** claimed **"decisive control"** and said US officials *"lie"*; **Araghchi** called the war a failure; the Foreign Ministry called the sanctions a **"crime against humanity."** The **White House** told *Al Jazeera* the Strait is **de-mined and safe for transit** and that no talks are occurring or scheduled. **Two irreconcilable transit counts were published on the same day and both are logged.** Trump said the **"Strait of Hormuz is open"** at **24 vessels a day** against ~130 pre-war; *Al Jazeera* counted **seven commodity ships** on Thursday, **down from 17**, against a **~100/day** baseline, with a six-month average of **seven a day**. **The six-month ledger is the fullest this audit has carried:** **4,350 killed and 12,510 injured in Lebanon**; **3,527 killed in Iran**; **60 Israelis**; **28 in the Gulf states**; **18 US service members killed and 757 wounded**; **3,580+** US/Israeli attacks on Iran and **2,053+** Iranian attacks in return; **70 confirmed ship attacks** with **19 seafarers killed**; **$37.5bn** in official US war costs against reported internal estimates of **$80-100bn**; **Brent +22%** from **$72.48** to **$88.58** after a **$120.88** peak; the **Strategic Petroleum Reserve at 290 million barrels — 41% of capacity and the lowest since 1982**; **Trump approval 33%** against 65% disapproval. **The Pentagon ledger published the same day is a depletion ledger.** More than **1,000 Patriot interceptors** expended — roughly **half the inventory**; more than **200 THAAD** — about **two-thirds of the stockpile**; at least **1,000 Tomahawks** — about **one-third**; with roughly **two years** to build each replacement. A US defence official told the *Associated Press* on **August 27** that European interceptor shortages caused by the Iran war are **"beyond critical"**, and NATO confirmed low Patriot inventories. Iranian attacks damaged US military infrastructure in **Bahrain**, the Fifth Fleet's major naval supply hub, forcing reliance on **Diego Garcia** and lengthening logistics. Retired General **Joseph Votel**: *"Iran's strategy is to extend the war in both time and geography, and frankly, they've succeeded."* Senator **Jack Reed** called the war a **"policy failure of historic consequence."** **Inside Iran:** **66% annual inflation**, foreign trade **down 35%** (**Pezeshkian**), a **15-million-litre daily gasoline deficit** (135m consumed against 121m produced), queues in Tehran and other cities, three rationing options under consideration, a **Kerman** price pilot abandoned within hours, and the rial above **2 million** to the dollar. **Mojtaba Khamenei** was quoted on *"the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment"* and against *"committing anything that harms social cohesion"* — three days after Trump called him **"very seriously wounded."** Attributed remarks are not a public appearance and the succession question is not resolved. **A twenty-eighth consecutive night passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran.** The war remains **air, naval, financial and judicial** — **no landing, no Kharg seizure, no draft order**. (Sources: *Fortune*, August 28, 2026; *Al Jazeera*, 'US-Israel war on Iran, six months down the line: In numbers,' August 28, 2026; *ABC News*, '6 months of war in Iran has left the Pentagon depleted and still fighting,' August 28, 2026; *CNBC* and *Associated Press*, August 28, 2026; Reuters via *NBC News*, August 28, 2026; *Al-Monitor*, August 28, 2026; *Just Security*, 'Early Edition: August 28, 2026.')

> **Daily update — August 28, 2026 (Day 183).** **The Strait that was declared cleared was attacked again, and the United States answered by building a court.** At **06:35 GMT on August 27** the **United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations** centre issued **Warning 121-26**: a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was **hit by an unknown projectile**, causing a fire since extinguished, with **no casualties, no environmental damage** and the crew reported safe. It was the **second vessel struck in the waterway this week**, and it came **thirty-six hours after** Trump declared every mine cleared from the Strait's international waters under a **"Zero Tolerance"** rule. **The distinction that matters is the weapon: a projectile, not a mine.** The demining claim is therefore not falsified by the attack, and the attack instead confirms Ambrey's **Alex Almeida**, quoted two days earlier, that mines *"have never been the primary threat."* Clearing the mines removed one instrument, not the danger. **The American move of the cycle was legal rather than military.** *Bloomberg* reported on **August 26** that the **Justice Department** is preparing to activate **maritime prize courts** — dormant since the **Second World War** and of negligible use since **1898** — to give federal prosecutors a faster route to condemn oil and other cargo taken from enemy or neutral vessels as **United States property**, to be sold with **proceeds transferred to the Treasury**. **Aaron Reitz**, the Houston-based US attorney whose office is partnering with department headquarters, confirmed DOJ is **"now reviving"** what he called an **"ancient body of maritime law."** The stated purposes are to **strengthen the blockade** and to **offset the cost of the conflict**; the reported trigger is that the civil-forfeiture route used against a seized Venezuelan supertanker has bogged down under third-party interventions. Plans are described as unfinalised. **For an audit tracking a predicted ground seizure, this is institutional evidence of a kind not previously available: a state that expects to resolve a chokepoint by taking it does not spend the interval rebuilding nineteenth-century admiralty procedure.** **Diplomacy moved, and then one government contradicted itself.** Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister **Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani** spent **August 27** in Tehran, meeting **Araghchi**, **Pezeshkian**, **Ghalibaf** and security chief **Mohsen Rezai** on the temporary corridor, the joint mine-clearing proposal and the conditions for renewed US-Iran dialogue — the **third mediator in four days** after Pakistan's **Asim Munir** on August 24 and Oman's **Badr Albusaidi** on August 25. Sheikh Mohammed: *"Dialogue and diplomatic solutions remain the optimal path for addressing disputes."* Rezai's answer did not move: Washington *"must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran's conditions"* — lift the naval blockade, unfreeze assets, remove oil sanctions. **And the corridor itself was put back in doubt from inside Iran.** A **senior Iranian source** told *Reuters* on **August 27** that the agreement with Oman over the Strait **"has not been finalized"** — one day after IRGC spokesman **Hossein Mohebbi** said the two states had agreed each country's share of the strait's waters and of its revenues. The audit logs the contradiction as internal to the Iranian state and does not resolve it. **Washington closed the door it had left ajar.** The White House said there are **"no talks or conversations"** going on or scheduled; **Trump**: *"We don't want to speak to them. We're not looking to meet or anything"*; Press Secretary **Karoline Leavitt**: the administration is *"continuing to pull every economic lever"* and *"the naval blockade continues to be in effect as well, which has proven hugely successful,"* with *"no negotiations... until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way"* and Iran's condition described as *"inflation is over 100%. They can't pay their police. They can't pay their military."* Reporting the same day indicated the administration **no longer seeks to revive the June 17 memorandum of understanding**. **The traffic data landed against the President's own number.** *Al Jazeera* published a dataset on **August 27** putting transits at **about five vessels a day between July 15 and August 23** against a pre-war baseline of about **100 a day** — a fall of **nearly 95%** — with **Gulf crude exports down 47%** from roughly 17m bpd to about 9m, **5-7m bpd** estimated disrupted, and port calls down **86% in Kuwait**, **69% in the UAE** (78 daily calls to 24), **66-68% in Qatar, Iraq and Bahrain** and only **15% in Saudi Arabia**. **Richard Matthews** of Gibson Shipbrokers: *"There is no alternative maritime route. There are some pipelines, but there's no alternative."* This sits against Trump's **August 26** claim on the Glenn Beck programme that **ten million barrels** passed through the Strait on Tuesday and that the waterway is *"functioning."* **Ten million barrels across about five hulls would require some two million barrels per vessel, roughly six times VLCC capacity**; the register carries the gap rather than adjudicating it. **Oil prints diverged within the same session and the divergence is logged, not resolved**: TradingEconomics carried Brent at **$89.48 (+2.12%)** while its own commentary described Brent *"slipping toward $87... a fourth straight session,"* and Fox carried crude *"near $82... a third consecutive day"* of losses. Every attributed cause is de-escalatory. **Inside Iran the fuel position was described as a red alert.** Executive Vice-President **Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah** said domestic production cannot meet consumption and the blockade prevents imports; strategic reserves are described internally as at **red alert** with stocks possibly exhausted within weeks; car queues blocked streets in **Tehran and Mashhad**; a price rise and rationing are signalled within weeks against tiers of 15,000 / 30,000 / 50,000 rials a litre; the rial holds near a record **2.06 million** to the dollar against an official ~1.5 million, with inflation near **90%** by Iran's own Statistical Center. *Iran International* reported disagreement between **Pezeshkian** and the **Revolutionary Guard** over drawing down the fuel reserve. **The war aim was stated in its maximal form by a third party**: former Mossad chief **Barnea** said there is *"no choice"* but to keep striking Iran *"until the regime falls — and it will fall,"* while **Ali Vaez** of the International Crisis Group asked whether Washington is running *"a zero-sum campaign aimed at collapsing the regime, or leverage towards an agreement"* — a question now entered in the open-questions register. **Lebanon**: the IDF struck Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon on **August 27** after two Hezbollah explosive drones targeted Israeli troops in the south-eastern security zone; the Lebanese Health Ministry reported **one woman killed and six wounded, including a child**. **Russia-Ukraine**: the agenda of **Ratcliffe's** unannounced **August 25** Moscow visit was disclosed — a warning against actions escalating tensions with **Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania** and a request that Russia **reduce military and economic support for Iran**, with US assessments holding that Moscow may test NATO with a limited operation or hybrid attack in coming years; **Peskov** confirmed the meeting was with Russian intelligence representatives and not Putin, who was briefed afterwards; **Trump** called the trip *"semi-routine."* Overnight into **August 27** Russia struck **Kyiv** and other cities with ballistic missiles and drones — six explosions in the capital inside a minute around 3 a.m., **at least seven injured**, targets including warehouses, ports and energy and industrial facilities per FM **Sybiha** — and Ukraine downed **seven ballistic missiles, one anti-ship cruise missile and about 90% of the drones**. Ukrainian drones forced the **NORSI** refinery at **Kstovo** — Russia's **fourth-largest refinery and second-largest gasoline producer** — to suspend crude processing, its **fifth drone-related shutdown in under five months**, with **all major Lukoil refineries** reported shut; a Ukrainian strike hit a **bus in Russian-controlled Luhansk, killing nine**. **US-China**: the administration is reported to be **considering sanctions against Chinese banks** doing business with Iran; the **Justice Department** announced Chinese state-linked intrusions (group **QTFY**) against federal agencies and hospitals over the past year; and **Pentagon officials** were reported concerned that a prolonged Iran conflict **could embolden China in the Indo-Pacific** — the overstretch thesis, attributed for the first time to serving officials in the department running the war. **Gulf**: a Greek-operated **Patriot** battery in Saudi Arabia launched **three missiles** and downed **three Houthi UAVs** over the **Yanbu** oil-refining region on **August 27**, its **third combat use** since the war began — placing the Red Sea terminus of the principal Saudi bypass under direct attack. **Ground rung**: the **carrier force is being rotated, not massed**. The **USS Abraham Lincoln** left CENTCOM on **August 22** after more than 200 days; the **USS George Washington** entered Fifth Fleet in the week of **August 20** to relieve it; and the **USS Theodore Roosevelt** will deploy from **San Diego within weeks**, on a deployment of **at least seven months with crews told to plan for eight**, to relieve the George Washington in turn — sustaining **one** carrier on station against the **two** CENTCOM cited in July and the **three** of April. The **USS Tripoli** is **in port at Sasebo, Japan**, outside CENTCOM. The **Boxer ARG** with the **11th MEU** remains **untasked in the Arabian Sea on its 59th day**. Automatic Selective Service registration is now dated to **December 18, 2026** — pool-building, not activation. **A twenty-seventh consecutive night passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran. Still air, naval, financial and now judicial: no landing, no Kharg seizure, no draft order.**

> **Daily update — August 27, 2026 (Day 182).** **A double cycle — the August 26 update was not run, so this consolidates August 25-27 — and the United States spent it making the Strait navigable rather than taking it.** **The week's most consequential report put a duration on the non-kinetic posture for the first time in 182 days.** On **August 25** *Axios*, citing US officials, reported that Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** has told several allied foreign ministers that **"for the time being"** the United States is **not expected to launch new strikes** against Iran and will focus on other means of pressure — without ruling out strikes if Iran attacks first — and that **a second official said the posture is expected to remain in place until after the midterm elections**, when another military campaign could again be considered. The named priorities were **sanctions, the naval blockade, and "moving ever-increasing amounts of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz."** **Three instruments, none of them a ground force.** **The instrument actually applied to the chokepoint was a robot and a contractor.** On **August 25** Trump announced that the US Navy has cleared **all mines** from the Strait's international waters and declared **"Zero Tolerance"** — *"Any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed"* — with the **Space Force** *"watching every square inch."* US officials confirmed the method: **underwater drones** scanned the Traffic Separation Scheme over recent months and located **more than 100 objects suspected to be mines**, and the military **contracted with private companies** to remove or detonate them; the CENTCOM operation began in **April**. Trump also said all **28 Iranian mine-laying boats** had been destroyed. Iran's **Gharibabadi** answered that *"no one except Iran knows the location"* and that the claim was *"only aimed at calming markets"*; **Mark Hilborne** (King's College London) gave the CENTCOM claim *"strong confidence"* for the main lanes while warning *"there may be risks beyond the lanes"*; **Alex Almeida** (Ambrey) said mines *"have never been the primary threat."* **War-risk insurance did not move** from 7.5-10% of hull value, and **traffic did not move either** — three transits on August 23 and two on August 24, the fewest since early May. **The Strait's future governance went into a document signed by Tehran and Muscat, not Washington.** Oman's FM **Badr Albusaidi** met **Araghchi** in Tehran on **August 25** and the two ministries announced a **"phased framework"** for a **joint temporary navigational corridor** and a **joint mine-clearing project**, with talks to continue toward a permanent corridor and **"the future administration of the Strait."** On **August 26** **Gharibabadi** gave the terms: **seven miles wide**, **entry beginning in Iranian territorial waters** with part of the exit also through them, **Iranian permission and surveillance required**, **military vessels barred**, **permanent arrangement in 30-60 days** — and *"the agreed-upon transit route with Oman is a temporary route,"* with full reopening conditioned on US compliance with the **June 17 MoU**, sanctions relief, release of frozen assets, an end to the war and **war-damage compensation**. IRGC spokesman **Hossein Mohebbi** said the two had agreed **"each country's share of the strait's waters and Iran and Oman's share of its revenues"** and that *"the Strait of Hormuz belongs to Iran and the Sultanate of Oman."* **Within a day the enforcement record contradicted the diplomacy:** Iran's shipping monitoring agency said the Indian tanker **HAANA** was warned to stop on that same southern route and turned back, and that **no vessel traffic had been observed on it in 24 hours** — against Kpler's **>80% Omani-route share**. **The market fell three sessions running:** Brent to about **$89** on August 25 (a one-week low) and about **$86** on August 26, WTI near **$80**, with BBH calling the sanctions **"more of a warning shot than a decisive blow."** **Trump removed the clock:** *"I have no time schedule, none. I'm not in a hurry"* (Al Jazeera, August 26); the Strait is *"a very functioning strait"* and Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** is not dead but *"very seriously wounded"* (Glenn Beck, August 26). **Inside Iran the petrol ran out:** station closures and queues across Tehran under a **20-litre limit**, a state body warning of a **"critical"** shortfall, Executive Vice-President **Ghaempanah** saying *"with the US naval blockade, we cannot import gasoline,"* **Pezeshkian** calling these *"the worst conditions of an economic war,"* and the rial at a record **2.06 million** to the dollar on August 25. **The ledger moved to 776 — 18 killed and 758 wounded** — with more than 90% of the newest additions Army, against a service split of 580+ Army, 86 Navy, 64 Air Force and **19 Marines** (~2.5% across 182 days); *The Intercept* restated the undercount dispute, including 200+ **USS Gerald R. Ford** fire casualties excluded and an April 21 WIA count that fell by 15 unexplained. **Elsewhere:** **CIA Director John Ratcliffe** made an **unannounced visit to Moscow** on August 25 — the first by a US spy chief since **Burns in November 2021** — meeting Russian intelligence counterparts, with **Peskov** saying Putin did not plan to meet him and that there were **no plans for talks with Witkoff or Kushner**; Washington had asked Kyiv to pause strikes on Moscow Monday-Wednesday. Russian attacks killed **four** and injured **95** across Ukraine over August 25-26 (163 drones, 132 downed, 18 locations), including an **FPV double-tap on rescue workers in Kramatorsk**. **Lin Jian** said China *"will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights"* and **Ghalibaf thanked Beijing** for declining to comply; Kpler puts Chinese imports of Iranian crude via Hormuz at **~530,000 bpd, 48% below pre-war**. **Kim Jong Un** presided over an August 25 politburo meeting on the economy that **did not mention Trump's overture**; today is the original end date of **Ulchi Freedom Shield's counteroffensive phase, which never took place**. **Qatar's Prime Minister arrives in Tehran today.** **A 25th and 26th consecutive night passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran. Still air, naval and financial only — no landing, no Kharg seizure, no draft order. The predicted US ground seizure remains DISCONFIRMED for a 182nd day.**

> **Daily update — August 25, 2026 (Day 180).** **The financial offensive arrived and it has a name.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** held his 2 p.m. ET news conference on **August 24** and unveiled **"Operation Economic Outcast"** — **five sectoral determinations** against **digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping**, with **nearly 60** Iran-linked people, entities and vessels designated across the **UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland**, **every country given a defined wind-down timeline**, **most secondary sanctions deferred behind a "cure period,"** and a **major financial institution signalled for designation by the end of the week**. The objective was stated without euphemism: **"It is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime."** The White House positioned the operation as the **"endgame" phase** succeeding Operation Epic Fury — *"Beginning today, the actions of Treasury and other agencies will tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue that funds the IRGC and the evil Iranian regime."* **Regime collapse is now a declared American war aim and the declared instrument is the banking system.** **The cycle's one counter-indicator is logged in full:** Secretary of War **Pete Hegseth** said the same day that military force is **not ruled out** in the Strait of Hormuz **"or anywhere else."** **The market marked the offensive down:** Brent **fell** on announcement day after a week of more than 5% gains — Reuters **-1.4% to ~$93**, CNBC **-2.5% to $92.06**, straits.live **$92.10 at -1.67%** — on profit-taking. **The rial went the other way,** hitting a record **2.02 million to the dollar** on the open market against an official rate of ~1.5m, with **rice up ~60%** and **beef up >150%** since February. **Tehran answered with dismissal plus a threat against host states:** Araghchi said Washington *"repeatedly put forward the same old plans"*; spokesman **Esmail Baghaei** said *"Any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences,"* *"Our hands are not tied,"* and that Iran has **the right to target any location used to launch attacks against it**, warning countries against providing territory or facilities to the United States. **Two tankers were hit in twenty-four hours:** the Saudi VLCC **Amzan** (Bahri) by **Houthi ballistic missiles and drones ~63nm west of Yanbu** in the Red Sea on August 24 — fire on the main deck, crew safe, described by **Yahya Saree** as a **"siege for siege"** operation against the Saudis; and an **unnamed tanker disabled in its engine room ~9nm northeast of Ash Shishah, Oman** at **0131 UTC on August 25**, unclaimed. **CENTCOM reached 71 redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded** as of August 24 — and disclosed for the first time that **more than 40 humanitarian aid vessels** have been permitted through. **The traffic picture acquired its first directional dataset:** CNN Business, citing **Kpler**, reports **more than 80% of liquids transits** over the preceding two weeks took the **Omani route** or were dark transits that likely did, concluding **Iran has lost significant control**; Gulf News puts southern-corridor traffic **up ~400% over two weeks to nearly 200 ships weekly**; straits.live still carries **one transit** against a **73-a-day baseline**, **370 hulls off berth**, **eight of nine major container carriers on the Cape route**, and **December 31 reopening odds at 34%**. **Diplomacy ran through Islamabad and Muscat:** Field Marshal **Asim Munir** and Interior Minister **Mohsin Naqvi** met Iranian Interior Minister **Eskandar Momeni** in Tehran on August 24, with the **June 17 Islamabad Memorandum's 60-day window having lapsed in mid-August without extension**; Oman's Foreign Minister **Sayyid Badr Albusaidi** arrives in Tehran on **August 25** to meet Araghchi. **A twenty-fourth consecutive night** passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran. **Pentagon casualties hold at 775** (18 killed, 757 wounded), and the **service split is new and pointed: 580+ Army, 86 Navy, 64 Air Force and 19 Marines** — the service that would carry an opposed landing has absorbed **2.5% of the wounded across 180 days**. **USNI's August 24 tracker confirms USS Abraham Lincoln has left CENTCOM** after almost seven months and is now in 7th Fleet, completing the relief that leaves **carrier presence at two**, the same number CENTCOM published in July. Pump **$4.0991**; diesel **$5.6134** at a further record. **Still air, naval and financial only — no landing, no Kharg seizure, no draft order. Predicted US ground seizure remains DISCONFIRMED for a 180th day.**

> **Daily update — August 2, 2026 (Day 157).** **The weekend the campaign was to begin passed without it.** The single most testable claim carried into this cycle was that a multi-day campaign against Iran's energy and civil infrastructure could start **"as soon as this weekend."** Through the end of **August 1** no US strike wave against Iranian territory was reported by any outlet, and the reporting verb moved backwards. *Al Jazeera* recorded that Trump **"had not yet authorized the potential two-week operation targeting Tehran's electricity grid,"** consistent with *CBS News*'s July 31 position that final authorisation had not been given and inconsistent with the *Wall Street Journal*'s framing that the order had been issued. *ABC News*, updating at 7:34 PM EDT on July 31, reported **CENTCOM had prepared a two-week air campaign** while **some administration officials favoured "a shorter, more severe salvo"** intended to advance negotiations rather than force capitulation — an internal argument **between two air options**, with no ground element re-entering the reporting. **The cycle's largest new fact is a ceiling, not a strike.** **CSIS** estimates **fewer than 827 Patriot interceptors** remain in US stocks against roughly **2,200 pre-war** of the two most-modernised variants, and **fewer than 278 THAAD** against **452** — **more than 60% of both expended** in five months of this war. **Three sources familiar with the matter told *CNN* the estimates are close to internal government figures.** Production runs at **183 THAAD a year** with roughly **three and a half years from contract signature to delivery**, and CSIS assesses **three or more years** to pre-war levels even against **$18.2 billion** allocated for Patriot, THAAD and Tomahawk within a **$67 billion FY2026 emergency funding proposal**. **Gen. Dan Caine** is reported to have **warned privately about the shortages**, cited as a restraint on broader strikes. CSIS's own framing is that the strategic risk is not sustaining this war but **responding to another high-intensity contingency before inventories are rebuilt**. **This is a ground-rung fact, not only an air-defence fact:** an amphibious or airborne lodgement on a mined island twenty miles off the Iranian coast must be covered against ballistic and cruise missile fire for as long as it is held, and the covering inventory is the depleted one. Specialists have identified **holding Kharg rather than taking it** as the binding problem since March; this cycle supplies the arithmetic. **Washington moved people instead of munitions.** On **August 1** US embassies in **at least ten Middle Eastern countries** — the UAE, Qatar, Oman, Iraq, Jordan, Israel, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Egypt — issued near-simultaneous alerts telling Americans to **"consider departing"** or **"be prepared to depart,"** citing **"the potential for unforeseen escalation"** and warning of flight cancellations and periodic airspace closures. That is a genuine escalation indicator and is logged as one — **and it is the inverse of a ground-operation signature**, which is inbound force flow rather than outbound civilians. No **ordered departure** of official personnel or dependents was announced, which is the more escalatory category and was not reached. **The Strait tightened without a decision.** Ship-tracking showed transits falling **77% in a single day, from 22 vessels to five**; the straits.live board at 22:59 UTC held **11% of normal** against an 88/day pre-crisis baseline, with **371 vessels holding position away from berth**, **36 tankers running AIS-dark**, **war-risk insurance at 8.0× pre-crisis** (~$2.5M per VLCC), eight of the nine largest container lines routing via the Cape, and **2% market-implied odds of reopening by August 15**. **UKMTO logged two tanker incidents in Omani waters** — an explosion 21nm NE of **Khasab** with no damage, and a projectile strike 11nm NE of **Limah** that damaged the engine room and left the vessel **not under command** — **both unattributed**. > **Daily update — August 1, 2026 (Day 156).** **The United States picked its instrument, and it is airpower against energy — not Marines against Kharg.** Four outlets reported the same coercive package on July 31. The *Wall Street Journal*, citing US officials, reported that **Trump has ordered another wave of strikes "with the aim of forcing the Islamic Republic's surrender,"** expected to last **several days** and able to begin **as soon as this weekend**. *CBS News* named the target classes: **power plants, refineries, electricity infrastructure across Tehran** (under high-level discussion, no Friday decision) and **bridges of dual military-civilian use** — with strikes possible throughout the weekend and discussion of **concluding before financial markets opened Monday**. The plan was raised at Trump's **Camp David cabinet meeting**, where he said: **"We'll be hitting them very hard. At some point, they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore.'"** One source said White House political aides **"were strongly opposed."** **The order's status is itself contested:** the WSJ reports it as ordered; CBS reports that **Trump has not given final authorisation**; *CNN*'s two officials say the strikes **could be called off**; and an Israeli official says **"Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran"** — against multiple US sources saying Israel had been notified and was coordinating. **Trump:** *"I'm losing faith in them because they do lie,"* while not ruling out a deal. **In none of the four reports does a ground element appear** — no landing, no embarkation, no MEU tasking, no airborne insertion, and **Kharg Island is not named**. That matters: the Kharg-seizure option prepared since March, built around two MEUs and 1,000-2,000 soldiers of the 82nd Airborne, existed to supply exactly the leverage this air campaign is now reported to be seeking. **Iran answered by drone, across the Gulf, against bases.** Its army and the IRGC claimed one-way attack drones against **Sheikh Isa Air Base** in Bahrain — which Iran called *"one of the most important US military installations in the Gulf region"* — and **Ahmad al-Jaber** and **Ali al-Salem** in Kuwait and **Al Azraq** in Jordan, targeting aircraft shelters, satellite communications, power generators, navigation systems and equipment storage, framing the Bahrain strike as revenge for an **Iranian Su-24 pilot killed in February**. Iran claimed **"significant damage"**; **no US or Bahraini comment followed** and no casualties were reported. **US wounded rose 32 to 685; KIA holds at 18.** **CENTCOM confirmed it is investigating** the Qeshm deaths of a **two-year-old and the child's parents**, a spokesman saying *"The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike Iranian forces."* **Damietta moved away from Tehran:** **Araghchi denied Iranian involvement** (*"Egypt is an important friend and partner in the region"*) and alleged an **Israeli false flag**, while **Egypt's Diaa Rashwan publicly rejected** a *WSJ* report that Cairo blames Iran, with drone debris under forensic analysis and Prime Minister **Madbouly** confirming the investigation. **Riyadh raised the coalition Washington could not:** Saudi Arabia's Defence Ministry convened **military representatives of 43 countries in Riyadh on July 30** for a **maritime defence coalition** headquartered in the kingdom, covering the **Bab al-Mandeb, Red Sea and Gulf of Aden**, with **thirteen public backers** (Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Yemen, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Sudan, Djibouti, Somalia) — in the same week Britain and France still refuse to co-lead Hegseth's Hormuz coalition. **Baghdad contradicted the President**, saying it had **no prior knowledge** of the July 28 US-Saudi strikes that Trump said were coordinated with Iraq, and suspended PM al-Zaidi's Riyadh visit. **A Russian Kh-101 detonated on NATO soil** near **Tarnawa-Kolonia** outside Lublin, leaving a **ten-metre crater**; NATO scrambled fighters, activated air defences and said it would **"defend territory."** **Brent rose 3.87% to $90.24, closing July up ~24% — its strongest month since March**; **diesel set another war high at $5.3530**, regular $4.1060. **Hormuz transits hit a two-week high of 28** as LNG traffic resumed after a fortnight, against throughput still assessed at **11% of normal**. **Still air and maritime only — no landing, no Kharg seizure, no relief ARG, no draft.** The predicted **US GROUND seizure remains DISCONFIRMED**, and this cycle strengthens that on evidence rather than on the passage of another day. > **Monthly scoring run — August 1, 2026.** **All 170 analysis files and 983 predictions/claims re-evaluated against the Day 156 record; currency web-verified across every tracked theatre (US-Iran, Russia-Ukraine, NATO-Russia, China-Taiwan, DPRK, Venezuela, Israel-Lebanon, US-China trade).** The independent sourcing this cycle **converges with the daily record rather than amending it**, and on the corpus's single most-loaded forecast it converges hard. The **Council on Foreign Relations Global Conflict Tracker**, surveying the war through July 29, records that **"no significant US ground force commitment is documented"** and that operations have **"remained primarily aerial and naval, with US military focus on air strikes and enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports."** That is a third-party, non-daily-cycle assessment reaching the same verdict this project has logged for 156 consecutive days. The CFR tally also gives the war's independent human ledger: **~1,701 documented civilian deaths in Iran, up to 3.2 million Iranians displaced**, a US strike on an Iranian school that killed at least 175, and Hegseth's cost figure of **~$37.5 billion** through late July. **On Kharg specifically, the open-source force estimate has not moved and the obstacle has hardened**: experts put the seizure requirement at **at least ~1,200 troops** — a Marine battalion landing team, a reinforced Army airborne battalion, or a combination — while Iran has laid **anti-personnel and anti-armour mines on the very shoreline an amphibious landing would use** and moved additional **MANPADS** onto the island; specialists note the binding problem is **holding** the island, not taking it. Planning has been documented since **March 25**; execution has never begun. **New this cycle and not in the morning daily:** **Poland did NOT invoke Article 4** after the **Kh-101** detonation near Lublin — Tusk attributed the missile to Russia on fragment analysis and convened an emergency coordination group, but Warsaw left the treaty mechanism alone pending investigation, a deliberate step *down* from its September 2025 response to the drone incursion, when it did invoke Article 4; NATO aircraft were reportedly **seconds from shooting the missile down** before assessing it would fall on its own, and nobody was hurt. **Venezuela's US-backed transition talks opened August 1** as scheduled with **Jorge Rodríguez** leading the government delegation and **Dinorah Figuera** the opposition, **María Corina Machado outside the room by her own choice** — she will not obstruct "real progress" and will judge the process on restored institutions, freed political prisoners and a scheduled election. **Israel-Lebanon trilateral talks are set for Rome, August 4-6**, working the late-June US-brokered framework — Hezbollah disarmament, LAF deployment south, phased Israeli withdrawal through two pilot zones. **China-Taiwan produced exercises, not escalation:** a **two-day PLA live-fire drill inside PRC territorial waters in the Taiwan Strait, July 23-24**, **Joint Sea-2026** with Russia off Qingdao **July 6-13**, a joint PRC-Russian air patrol into South Korea's ADIZ, and PLA ground personnel training at a Russian complex on drone-saturated warfare — no blockade, no quarantine, no invasion. **DPRK stayed on the naval track:** Kim observed a **strategic cruise-missile launch and anti-ship, anti-submarine and air-defence evaluations aboard the new 5,000-tonne destroyer *Kang Kon*** (tests July 3, reported July 5), ahead of the ship's induction within two months — no nuclear test, no ICBM launch. **On the draft rung: there is no US draft, and this cycle the indicator moved BACKWARDS.** The statutory mandate is unchanged — automatic registration of men aged **18-26** must begin **December 19, 2026** under the December 2025 NDAA — and web sourcing confirms the switch to automatic registration is scheduled for the end of 2026, removing the registrant's opportunity to object at the point of registration. But the implementing rulemaking was **withdrawn**: on **July 23, 2026 the Selective Service System pulled the proposed automatic-registration rules** it had sent to the White House on March 30, after nearly four months without action, with no explanation and no re-proposal. A registration mechanism is not a mobilisation, and conscription still requires both Congress and the President. **US troop levels in the Middle East remain above 50,000** — roughly 10,000 above the standing presence, after the deployment of 2,500 Marines and 2,500 sailors. **Net status changes this cycle are few and all in the direction of the existing record**, because the July daily cycle had already scored the war's turns as they happened; the corpus's ground-invasion forecasts stay **DISCONFIRMED**, and this month strengthens that verdict on evidence: the coercive package reported on July 31 seeks Iranian capitulation **through cumulative destruction from the air against power plants, refineries, Tehran's grid and dual-use bridges** — precisely the leverage the Kharg seizure option was designed to supply — and **no ground element appears in any of the four independent accounts of it.** The Kharg option has now been available, staffed and repeatedly reported for **four months** without being taken, while the mission it was meant to accomplish has been reassigned to airpower. > **Daily update — July 31, 2026 (Day 155).** **The United States went back to bombing Iran itself.** After six days in which no American munition touched Iranian territory — and one in which the retaliation for an Iranian ballistic strike was routed to **Iraq** instead — US Central Command announced overnight that it had **"successfully completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran,"** striking **"dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities."** The operation ran roughly **two hours** and a US official told the *Jerusalem Post* it was **"about twice the size of the previous"** bombardment. **The target map is a coastline:** Bandar Abbas, **Qeshm Island**, **Kish Island**, **Abu Musa**, three cities of **Bushehr** province, **Kazerun** and **Farashband** in Fars, and **Abadan** and **Ahvaz** in Khuzestan, where seven locations were struck and power went out. **Kharg Island was NOT on the reported list.** **The cost fell on civilians:** IRNA said **three killed and two wounded on Qeshm**, reported by *Al Jazeera* as **a couple and their two-year-old child**, with children aged seven and nine wounded and two more trapped under rubble; three IRGC personnel were also reported killed. **Iran promised same-day retaliation and claimed the Strait:** the IRGC said **"with the help of God Almighty, the aggressor will be punished today,"** warned that states aiding the US would **"receive a harsh response,"** and asserted it retains **"full control"** of Hormuz, where **"a stranger who has come from thousands of kilometres away will not be allowed to interfere."** **It also claimed three F-35s destroyed at Al Azraq** — the Jordanian base also known as Muwaffaq Salti — **and US personnel killed. CENTCOM denied the aircraft categorically and said nothing about the personnel**, with the *Washington Times* reporting an unanswered request for clarification. **The war widened to two new places.** Kuwait's Ministry of Defence said an Iranian strike hit a building belonging to a **Chinese company** in the country's north, **killing one worker** — spokesman **Saud Al-Atwan** calling it **"Iranian aggression."** And an **unclaimed drone** struck the **US-owned FSRU Energos Winter** at **Egypt's Damietta** at ~14:20 UTC July 29, spreading fire to the LNG carrier **Gaslog Salem**; crews evacuated, no injuries, **Egypt's cabinet confirmed a drone and named no one**, and **Trump blamed Iran without evidence**. It is the **first attack on Egyptian soil of the war** and the first on an energy **IMPORT** terminal — extending the energy war from the export chokepoint to the receiving end, on the Mediterranean. **Riyadh fought and sued for peace in consecutive days:** Defence Minister **Prince Khalid bin Salman** met Trump and Vance on July 29, hours after Saudi jets flew alongside CENTCOM in Iraq, carrying MBS's message — self-defence, but **diplomacy is "a more fruitful path"** and **Netanyahu is the one pushing escalation** — while lobbying for **F-35s**. **Baghdad hardened:** the National Security Council under PM **Ali al-Zaidi** called the July 28 strikes **"a flagrant violation of Iraq's sovereignty and the sanctity of its lands,"** the presidency called them an attack on **"official security institutions,"** and the foreign ministry summoned **both** the US chargé d'affaires and the Iranian ambassador. **Markets:** Brent eased below **$90** ($89.45, −1.11%) after a **7.9% surge** on July 29; **diesel set another war high at $5.339** and regular rose to **$4.098**. **The straits.live readings broke comparability** (35 transiting / 1,357 stranded / 9 dark against 10-13 / 339 / 68 a day earlier, with no methodology note) and are recorded as printed and flagged; IMF PortWatch's independent baseline is unchanged at **10 transits vs 88/day**. **GROUND RUNG — the first ambiguous signal in a week, and still zero on every execution indicator.** The declared target categories — coastal surveillance, coastal defence, maritime capability — and the littoral strike map are **exactly the suppression the Pentagon's reported limited raids on Kharg and coastal weapons sites would require**, and **equally the whole objective of a navy running a blockade and escorting convoys**. The strike list cannot distinguish them, and this project records it as an **ambiguous shaping signal, not intent**. Against it: **Kharg was not struck**, no landing, **no new ARG/MEU or ground-formation order**, **Boxer ARG still the sole deployed ARG fleet-wide** with **Tripoli home in Sasebo and no relief nine days on**, **~50,000 personnel unchanged**, and the **Selective Service rule still withdrawn** since July 23 with no re-proposal. **Predicted US GROUND seizure remains DISCONFIRMED for a 155th day.** (CENTCOM public release; *Al Jazeera*; CNBC; NBC News; *The Hill*; *The Jerusalem Post*; *The Washington Times*; Al Arabiya English; *Business Recorder*; *The National*; Seatrade Maritime; Euronews; *Just Security*; Semafor; Rudaw; straits.live; AAA, July 29-30, 2026.)

> **Daily update — July 30, 2026 (Day 154).** **The war resumed on three rungs at once, and the American retaliation landed in Iraq with Saudi jets alongside — not on Iranian soil, and not by ground.** **Iran claimed what it had refused to claim a day earlier:** the **IRGC** said its air force had targeted **Muwaffaq Salti Air Base** and a **CENTCOM centre** in Jordan, where air defences intercepted **five missiles**, and framed it as open-ended — **"As long as threats against the Islamic Republic of Iran continue and illegal and vicious actions by American forces against our interests continue, the resistance will continue."** No US casualties. The attribution is now bilateral and on the record, where the prior cycle had only the American account. **The IRGC then struck and stopped THREE TANKERS in the Strait of Hormuz** — its first claimed shipping strikes since the July 24-26 halt — saying the vessels **"continued to move along an unsafe and illegal route, ignoring our warnings"**; Tasnim carried it as *Three Trespassing Vessels Stopped in Strait of Hormuz*. That formally triggers Trump's **July 22 doctrine** of destroying **one Iranian bridge or power plant per ship attacked**, which had **not been invoked** by the cycle close. **Trump promised a heavy answer in categorically unspecific terms:** Iran is **"going to get a beating"**; **"we'll be hitting them hard"**; the US had **"destroyed most of"** Iran and would **"finish the job."** **What the United States actually did was strike Iraq.** CENTCOM announced that it **"and the Saudi Arabian Armed Forces conducted precision strikes in Iraq, July 28, against Iran-aligned terrorists that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) directed to attack U.S. forces and Saudi energy infrastructure"** — **multiple logistics hubs and weapons storage sites**, after **more than 30 IRGC-directed drone attacks in 72 hours** (and 600+ attempted attacks on US personnel February-April). **It is the first time Riyadh has claimed strikes inside Iraq since the war began.** Maj. Gen. **Turki Al-Maliki** confirmed coordination and said Saudi air defences had **"intercepted and destroyed multiple drones launched from Iraqi territory aimed at vital petroleum facilities in the Kingdom's Eastern Province and Riyadh region"**; the defence ministry invoked **Article 51**, said the Kingdom **"does not seek escalation but will respond to any aggression it faces,"** and reserved the right to act **"at the appropriate time and place."** **Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces said at least 20 members were killed and 32 wounded** across sites reported in **Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala and Diyala**, calling it **"a highly dangerous escalation"** and a violation of Iraqi sovereignty and of **"official security institutions"**; the Iraqi presidency **"categorically rejected any attacks in Iraqi territory"** while also opposing **"the use of Iraqi territory as a launching point,"** and PM **Ali al-Zaidi** convened an emergency security meeting. Iran's foreign ministry condemned **"aggressive attacks."** **The Hormuz governance track went backwards.** Iran **rejected** Oman's Gulf-backed plan; deputy FM **Kazem Gharibabadi** described the offer — **"Oman proposed to us the creation of a route in the Strait of Hormuz, with 50 percent of it located in our territorial waters and 50 percent in Omani territorial waters,"** funded by **voluntary** contributions on the **Malacca** model (~$70m/yr) — and Iran's counterplan: **"Our proposal is for one route to lie entirely within the territorial waters of the Islamic Republic of Iran, with part of the other route also passing through Iranian territorial waters,"** with oversight of **both inbound and outbound** traffic and a reported **$1 MILLION PER SHIP** "service fee" for reconstruction. He tied it to war aims — **"If the Strait of Hormuz returns to its previous state, our success in this war is not complete"** — argued the June 17 MOU obliged Iran to give free passage **"for only 60 days,"** denied Iran had sought talks (**"there was no begging from the Iranian delegation"**, no direct request in **15 days**), and drew the sharpest maritime tripwire of the war: **"if they bring equipment or any vessel… for mine-clearing operations near the Strait of Hormuz, they will be considered legitimate targets."** **The coalition Washington wants is not forming: BRITAIN AND FRANCE declined to lead it.** POLITICO reported **Hegseth** urging the UK and France to help lead the Hormuz naval mission, with UK Defence Minister **Wes Streeting** assisting, and that European allies are refusing **"until they see an enduring ceasefire in the Iran war"** — four British officials and one US official said no movement was expected soon. **REUTERS: CHINA TO SHIP UP TO 400 MANPADS TO IRAN WITHIN WEEKS** — 300-400 **QW-12/FN-16** launchers worth **$60-70m** via the Hong Kong intermediary **Zhongqing Baoshang International Investment**, routed **Urumqi → Pakistan**; Beijing: **"The relevant reports are completely groundless"**; Pakistan's military: **"absolutely concocted and false."** **Markets reversed:** Brent jumped back **above $90** (straits.live **$90.40, +3.43%**) after a July 28 close reported at **$84.09 (−4.8%)**, ending a three-session, ~$14 slide from the July 23 settle of $100.69; pump **$4.091** regular and **$5.329** diesel — **another diesel war high**, rising through the entire crude decline. **The backlog eased a second day** from a still-closed baseline: **339** vessels stranded (from 405), **68** tankers dark (from 77), with PortWatch still at **10 transits vs an 88/day baseline (~11%)**. **Casualties:** a Pentagon official said **"Operation Epic Fury has concluded"** as the rationale for the new **"Overseas Operations"** category but **would not give an end date**; **total wounded across both categories is now 642**. **THE GROUND RUNG NOT ONLY HELD AT ZERO — TWO OF ITS PRECONDITIONS REGRESSED.** The **Selective Service withdrew its proposed automatic draft-registration rule on July 23** after the White House sat on it for nearly **four months** without acting and without comment (the **December 19, 2026** statutory deadline is unchanged; no rule is now pending; no draft has been called) — the **first backward movement on the draft indicator of this war** — and the only force generation actually under way, an **allied naval escort coalition**, was refused by both governments asked to lead it. **Still air/maritime only — no landing, no Kharg seizure, no relief ARG, no draft. Predicted US GROUND seizure remains DISCONFIRMED.** *(CENTCOM public release; Al Jazeera; IranWire; Tasnim; Bloomberg; CNBC; CBS News; Democracy Now; Just Security; POLITICO/E&E News; Reuters via U.S. News; Muscat Daily; The Week; Antiwar.com; AP via KSAT; straits.live; AAA, July 23-29, 2026.)*

> **Daily update — July 29, 2026 (Day 153).** **The strike pause broke — and it broke from Tehran, on the ballistic rung, fully intercepted.** At **5:45 p.m. ET on July 28** US Central Command said **Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces "launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on U.S. forces"** in the Middle East and that **"all Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted,"** with US forces **"vigilant and at a high state of readiness."** CENTCOM named neither the number nor the target; initial estimates were of **no more than four missiles**, with a reported trajectory toward a **US base in Jordan**. **No US casualties, and Iran issued no claim or explanation** — unlike its publicised July 9 and July 17 attacks on Jordan. It ended four days of two-sided quiet and reversed a kinetic indicator that had been falling since July 24, but it moved on the **BALLISTIC/AIR rung: no ground contact, no landing, no territorial move by either side.** **Hours earlier Trump hosted Netanyahu at the White House** — their first meeting since the war began on February 28 — after publicly rebuffing the Israeli briefing campaign on **Pickaxe Mountain**: **"I don't need Bibi to tell me that… Bibi's telling me that because he wants me to stay involved,"** and **"Why didn't you just tell it to me, why did you have to announce it to the world?"** The closed-door session ran just over an hour with **Vance, Rubio and Bessent** present and reporters excluded; **Karoline Leavitt** called it **"positive and productive,"** a senior Israeli source **"an excellent and comprehensive discussion on the key issues of the day, first and foremost Iran"** with an **"ironclad commitment"** that Iran never obtain nuclear weapons, and **Netanyahu "one of the best we've ever had."** Israel's public-diplomacy chief **Tzipi Hotovely** then said Pickaxe **did not come up** and that **"the idea that we have some intelligence here is a sort of fake news that ran throughout the day"** — while Trump said publicly, **"We took out their nuclear sites and we'll have to take out Pickaxe. If we don't make a deal, we don't make a deal. We'll take it very easily."** On the war's terms: **"If they don't make a deal then I go back and I finish the job."** Senior US officials called the Israeli collection **"amazing"** but said Jerusalem **"sees what it wants to see"** and described Netanyahu as **"seeking another escalation against Iran, even if he avoids saying so explicitly."** CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — see `netanyahu-pickaxe-intelligence-escalation-july-2026`. **At the chokepoint Trump claimed a NAVAL victory, not a territorial one:** **"We control the Strait. Our navy is incredible. Not one ship has gotten to Iran during any blockade,"** with CENTCOM's tally rising to **18 commercial vessels stopped** from entering or exiting Iranian ports, **2 disabled, 2 boarded**, enforced by **more than 20 warships**. **The Hormuz governance track acquired a concrete instrument:** Oman has put a **Gulf-backed plan for joint regional management** of the Strait to Tehran and carried it to Washington, drawing on the **Malacca Strait/Singapore model of VOLUNTARY industry contributions**, and a person familiar with the US position said the proposals as delivered contain **no mandatory transit tolls**. **Anna Kelly:** "President Trump has been clear that Iran cannot toll the Strait, which is an international waterway." **Rubio:** "No country is allowed to charge tolls or fees on an international waterway. That's existing international law." **Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi** said Iran will take **"any action"** to maintain control of the Strait and repeated that Tehran has **not requested negotiations** with the United States. **Iran issued two irreconcilable casualty tolls the same day:** government spokesperson **Fatemeh Mohajerani** put **more than 350 government employees** killed in the line of duty and said **Bushehr Airport** had been **"completely knocked out of service,"** while Health Minister **Mohammad-Reza Zafarghandi** put the toll from recent southern strikes at **60**. **The Intercept** reported Iran has fired **8,000-9,000 drones and missiles since February**, that **at least nine US outposts have been struck since July 9** with several sustaining significant damage, that **Patriot and THAAD stocks are three or more years from recovery** after **11,000+ munitions in the first 16 days**, and that the Pentagon **drastically understates casualty figures** — a second independent line on the July 26 reclassification. **Markets:** Brent slipped a **third** session to about **$86.58 (−1.54%)**, a far shallower move than the prior two, with straits.live at **$87.66**; the launch came after pricing. **Pump prices split:** AAA regular eased to **$4.099** while **diesel set another war high at $5.321**. **The shipping backlog eased for the first time of the resumed phase:** **405 vessels stranded** (from 426) and **77 tankers dark** (from 97), with **13 tankers transiting** — against PortWatch's 10 transits on July 23 and an 88/day baseline, about **11% of pre-crisis throughput**. **GROUND RUNG — UNCHANGED FOR A 153RD DAY, AND THE DAY WAS ITS CLEANEST DIRECTIONAL TEST:** the pause broke upward in intensity but on the ballistic rung and from the Iranian side; every US escalation option stated on the record was an **air** option against a nuclear site; **The War Zone's July 28 fleet count confirms USS Boxer (LHA-4) as the SOLE DEPLOYED amphibious ready group fleet-wide**, with **USS Tripoli back in Sasebo** after disembarking the 31st MEU at Okinawa and **no relief ARG announced six days on**; carriers *Abraham Lincoln* and *George H.W. Bush* remain in 5th Fleet. No US troops in Iran, no landing, no Kharg seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; ~50,000 personnel unchanged. **The predicted US GROUND seizure of Hormuz/Kharg remains DISCONFIRMED.** (CENTCOM via CBS News/CNN/ABC News/Fox News Digital live blogs; *The Times of Israel*; *Ynetnews*; *Jewish Insider*; *The Washington Times*; AGBI; NBC News; IranWire; *The Intercept*; The War Zone; TradingEconomics; straits.live; AAA Fuel Prices, July 28, 2026.)
