> **Daily update — July 28, 2026 (Day 152).** **The pause held a third day and the escalation option that reached the President was declined.** No US strikes and no Iranian retaliation for a third consecutive day — the longest two-sided quiet of the resumed phase — and reporting compiled in *Just Security*'s July 27 Early Edition recorded that **the Pentagon presented Trump with a plan for a 14th consecutive night of strikes and he did not authorise it**, preferring to let negotiations run. **Trump paired patience with an explicit air-resumption threat:** "I have a lot of patience. I have plenty of time. Plenty of time," and "I think there is a good chance that something could happen. If it doesn't, **we go back to doing what we were doing two days ago**" — with strikes resuming at greater force than before. To *Axios*: **"We are in very deep talks with Iran. If they don't work out, we will go back to very strong military action,"** and on the window, **"Not much time. Either it goes fast or not at all."** On stockpiles: **"We have plenty. We have a lot of ammunition. Different types."** **A flat factual split opened on whether talks exist at all:** Iranian foreign ministry spokesman **Esmail Baqaei** said Iran **"currently have no negotiations with the United States"** and that **"the discussions we have had over the past few days have been exclusively with Oman"**; deputy FM **Kazem Gharibabadi** said Washington had presented **"extreme demands"** Iran rejected, calling Tehran's posture **"dignified diplomacy."** The AP, citing regional officials, reported **Qatar- and Pakistan-led mediators making significant progress** toward restoring negotiations and reviving the collapsed interim ceasefire. **Iran's joint military command escalated rhetorically against the BLOCKADE, not a landing:** the **Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters** said the US naval blockade **"will be regarded as an expansion of the war in the region,"** citing three days of US threats against Iranian vessels, commercial ships and oil tankers in Iran's coastal and territorial waters, and warned the armed forces **"will not leave unanswered any threat or hostile action."** **The force generation that DID move is maritime and multinational:** the US and UK are convening a high-level **London conference** this week on an international coalition to protect Hormuz shipping, with **Hegseth and Gen. Dan Caine** possibly attending and participating governments to be asked for military equipment **and personnel** — allied naval escort forces, not US ground forces. **Markets extended the relief rally:** Brent fell a second straight session into the **$85-90** range (TradingEconomics $90.28, −8.23%; UPI close $88.36, −8.7%; CBS −6.8% to $85.49; straits.live $87.76), with WTI around **$82.6**, a two-session fall of roughly $10-15 from the July 23 settle of $100.69. **Pump prices did not follow:** AAA held at **$4.110 regular** and **$5.296 diesel**. **Hormuz stayed shut:** 426 vessels stranded, 97 tankers running dark, 14 tankers transiting, and **24 tankers waiting off Kharg Island** (up from 21). **Domestic support hit its wartime low:** a Reuters/Ipsos poll released July 27 found **just one in three Americans back the war**, with **69% saying Trump has failed to explain its goals**, though his overall approval ticked up three points to **37%**. **Netanyahu flew out secretly** from Nevatim Air Force Base aboard *Wings of Zion* amid a reported Iranian security threat for an 11 a.m. Tuesday July 28 meeting — his first with Trump in over five months — while **Zelensky** arrives the same day with an **air-ceasefire proposal**. **GROUND RUNG — UNCHANGED FOR A 152ND DAY, AND THE NEGATIVE EVIDENCE IS THE STRONGEST OF THE WAR:** no US troops in Iran, no landing, no Kharg seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; 50,000+ personnel unchanged; the July 22 Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU departure **remains unreversed with no relief ARG announced**; and *Foreign Policy*'s July 24 survey of former US commanders found the US **"does not appear to be moving toward a major ground operation in Iran,"** which would require far more than the ~50,000 troops in theatre — retired **Gen. Joseph Votel**: **"What we might see is the use of ground forces in limited raids that are going after key locations."** **The corpus-predicted US GROUND seizure of Hormuz/Kharg remains DISCONFIRMED.** (Reuters via France24; CBS News; CNBC; NPR; American Bazaar/AP; *Just Security*; WANA; Iran International; *Axios*; *Foreign Policy*; Reuters/Ipsos via Al-Monitor; TradingEconomics; UPI/Yahoo Finance; straits.live; AAA; *The Times of Israel*; Kyiv Post, July 24-27, 2026.)

> **Daily update — July 27, 2026 (Day 151).** **The pause became two-sided and two nights long.** No US strikes were reported overnight into Sunday July 26 — a second consecutive quiet night after thirteen — and a Defense Department source told CNN that operations are **"on a hold."** Iran matched it publicly: army spokesman **Mohammad Akraminia** said on state television, **"Since our strategy has essentially been retaliatory, we have also halted our retaliatory operations,"** and Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait reported no Iranian attacks overnight. **The reported rationale is capability-side, not diplomatic alone:** *Axios* reported that CENTCOM commander **Gen. Brad Cooper** told the White House that two weeks of strikes around the Strait had **"significantly degraded"** Iran's ability to target commercial vessels and that the designated targets were **"mostly exhausted"**; **Gen. Dan Caine** warned that **"a dwindling supply of air defence intercept"** could expose US personnel and allies; **VP JD Vance** also cautioned against escalating at the July 24 White House meeting. **The administration paired de-escalation with non-foreclosure:** UN Ambassador **Mike Waltz** said the pause was **"giving diplomacy some space,"** that talks run **"at the highest levels, all the way down to the technical levels,"** that Oman is **"engaging in a helpful way"** — and, rebutting shortage reporting, **"Not only do we have what we need in theater, there's more moving into theater,"** adding **"I'm not going to take that option off the table for the president."** Trump denied any munitions shortage and posted AI-generated images depicting attacks on Iranian facilities. **The Iran-Oman channel firmed:** the two countries' deputy foreign ministers met in Tehran July 24-25 and exchanged views on **"shared principles and operational mechanisms for managing the safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while respecting the sovereign rights of the two coastal states"**; spokesman **Esmail Baghaei** reported progress while saying the Strait's status **"remains unchanged."** A senior Iranian source told Reuters there is **"more skepticism than optimism,"** the halt being read as **"tactical rather than genuine."** **The blockade did not pause** — "in full effect," with 12 vessels redirected, 2 disabled and 2 boarded, the IRGC separately stopping six with warning shots and one tanker reported to have struck a mine. **Traffic effectively stopped:** Windward recorded **ONE vessel — a Comoros-flagged general cargo ship, outbound — and ZERO tankers in either direction** in the 24 hours to July 25, with a 12-hour window of no crossings at all; under 2% of the 88/day pre-crisis baseline and the lowest reading of the war. **Markets read de-escalation:** Brent fell more than 5% to about **$91/bbl** (TradingEconomics: $91.45, −7.05%), the sharpest one-day drop of the resumed phase, while AAA pump prices hit war highs of **$4.111 regular and $5.295 diesel**. **The Pentagon cut its own casualty series:** the official Iran-war toll fell from **18 killed / 482 wounded to 14 / 420**, with four July deaths and 207 wounded moved into a new **"Overseas Operations"** category dated from July 7 — changes the department called **"anomalies"** and a **"temporary data disruption."** **Ukraine opened a Caspian front against Iranian military cargo:** Zelensky confirmed strikes on a Russian warship and **"vessels used in military cargo shipments involving Iran,"** killing an Iranian sailor; Araghchi called it a **"blatant UN Charter violation"** carried out **"at Israel's behest"** that **"cannot go unanswered,"** and Zelensky alleged Russia feeds Iran satellite imagery of Gulf states and US facilities. **Domestically,** CBS News/YouGov (2,193 adults, July 22-24) found **67% want the conflict ended now**, war approval at **35%**, and 58% expecting months or years; Sen. **John Kennedy (R-LA)** said **"I don't think we need to send in troops,"** Sen. **Bernie Sanders** called the war **"unconstitutional… illegal."** Netanyahu meets Trump at the White House **Tuesday July 28**. **GROUND RUNG — UNCHANGED, AND THE AMPHIBIOUS RUNG FELL FOR THE FIRST TIME:** no US troops in Iran, no Kharg landing or seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; 50,000+ personnel unchanged — but the **Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group** (USS Tripoli LHA-7, USS New Orleans LPD-18, USS Rushmore LSD-47) completed its deployment and **offloaded ~2,500 Marines of the 31st MEU at White Beach, Okinawa on July 22** after four months under CENTCOM, **with no relief ARG announced** — removing the very unit the Pentagon's reported raid-and-seizure options had named, and leaving the Boxer ARG / 11th MEU as the theatre's sole amphibious group. **The corpus-predicted US GROUND seizure of Hormuz/Kharg remains DISCONFIRMED.** (Al Jazeera; > **Daily update — July 26, 2026 (Day 150).** **The thirteen-night US air campaign STOPPED: Iran reported its first night without US strikes ("Iran had a peaceful night" — Health Ministry spokesman Hossein Kermanpour), and US Central Command announced no strikes and declined comment when contacted — the first fall in the war's kinetic indicator since the resumed phase began.** **Trump paired escalation and de-escalation in one breath:** the US is **"locked and loaded"** for a major strike, but the threatened **"massive" attack "may be unnecessary"** because talks continue — Iranian negotiators, he said, **"are being by far the most serious that we've seen them"** ("that doesn't mean we get there"), Washington could still escalate **"to a much higher level,"** and the bottom line is unchanged: **"They cannot have a nuclear weapon."** *The Jerusalem Post* reported he has **not decided** on large-scale attacks — **"finger on trigger."** **Two mediation channels opened:** an **Omani delegation arrived in Tehran** (July 24) to discuss **"appropriate mechanisms for managing ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz"** (IRNA) — the Iran-Oman co-administration formula Washington and the Gulf states reject — and **Pakistan, encouraged by China,** explored a route back to US-Iran talks, with momentum from Iranian Interior Minister **Eskandar Momeni's** second Islamabad visit in under two weeks. **The war's kinetic centre migrated to the Red Sea:** the **Houthis fired "dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones" at Saudi Aramco facilities in JIZAN (refinery ablaze; CNN-geolocated fires) and YANBU** — the Kingdom's principal remaining crude corridor with Hormuz shut — in retaliation for a **Saudi-led coalition strike on Hodeidah port, its telecommunications infrastructure and Kamaran Island** that Riyadh's Maj. ## Quick Reference: Disconfirmed Claims

| Claim | Reality |
|-------|---------|
| “A president who has named the fall of the Iranian government as a war aim is preparing the ground force to accomplish it” | **He called the war “small potatoes” and said it is already essentially done.** On **September 4** Trump said the campaign is *“small potatoes”* and *“not a big thing”* for the United States and that *“we took over Venezuela and we have essentially taken over Iran”* — a claim of possession advanced on **Day 191 with no American soldier on Iranian soil**, and one whose direction is unambiguous: **no ground campaign has ever been launched by an administration simultaneously arguing that its war is small and already substantially won.** Force posture unchanged at ~50,000 troops and 19 warships; no new brigades, no new amphibious lift, no mobilisation, no call-up. |
| “The war's largest strike wave was conducted with precision that made civilian casualties improbable” | **The single worst incident in it was a direct hit on a house full of civilians, and the theatre commander is investigating it.** *Reuters'* four weapons experts — **Gareth Collett**, **Trevor Ball**, **Sebastian Schutte** and a fourth — all concluded that the **Kuhestak** strike was a **direct hit by a US munition**, not secondary damage from a ricochet off the telecommunications tower **135 metres away**; the **New York Times** and **BBC** identified a **US Precision Strike Missile**. The toll reached **five**, with nearly **seventy wounded**, most of them women and children. **CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper ordered an internal review** and the **Iranian Red Crescent** filed with the **ICC**. **Precision is not the same as discrimination, and this reference records both that the wave's total civilian toll — 18 killed — was far below corpus predictions of mass casualties, and that its worst single incident is now attributed to an American weapon.** |
| “Army Secretary Dan Driscoll's departure is contested and he may remain through the midterms” | **This reference's own September 4 claim, and it is withdrawn.** Driscoll's **official last day was Wednesday**, and on **Thursday** Trump named **Adam Telle** — the Army's **civil works** assistant secretary — **acting Secretary of the Army, effective immediately**. **The September 3 record that the departure had been effected was correct.** The underlying signal is unchanged: an acting, unconfirmed civilian secretary from a civil-works and legislative background, **no Senate-confirmed Chief of Staff**, and **more than 80 flag officers fired or blocked**. |
| “South Korea is deploying the Cheonghae Unit to the Strait of Hormuz — the first new allied military contribution of the war” | **This reference's own September 4 claim, and it is withdrawn to untested.** On **September 4** the South Korean government said publicly that a **review of options including military measures remains in progress and no decision has been made.** The options now reported are a **maritime patrol aircraft**, a **logistics support vessel** and a **mine detection and clearance unit** — **not** the 4,400-tonne destroyer ***Wang Geon*** and its naval special warfare boarding team. Expansion requires **both a government decision and National Assembly approval**. **A reported preparation is not a decision, and this theatre has now produced two consecutive cycles in which the difference mattered.** |
| “Iran would mount a large-scale attack on Israel if Israel took the Ali al-Taher ridge” | **The ridge fell and nothing followed.** The IDF's **36th Division** took **“operational control”** of the position **above and below ground** on **September 4**, clearing the two-decade Iranian-planned and Iranian-funded headquarters of **Hezbollah's Badr Unit**. Iran had reportedly warned Washington that this seizure would trigger a large-scale attack on Israel. **Through the cutoff there was no such attack, and Israel was not among Iran's named targets for a fourth consecutive cycle.** |
| “Iran can sustain a multi-front missile campaign against US regional bases” | **There was no third night, and the second night hit nothing.** After launches against Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, the UAE and Erbil on two consecutive nights, **no Iranian launches were reported on September 4**. A US official said the September 3 strikes *“didn't impact any military facilities in the Middle East where U.S. forces are based.”* No host government reported casualties or damage. **ISW-CTP assesses that the roughly 50% failure rate of Iranian ballistic missiles fired at Jordan may reflect degraded longer-range missile capabilities**, and the September 3 operation was conducted by the **Artesh**, not the IRGC. |
| “Kuwait's invocation of Article 51 means a Gulf state is about to enter the war” | **A right reserved is not a right exercised.** Kuwait cited **UNSCR 2817** by number and invoked **Article 51** to assert its **“full right... to take all necessary measures”** — the standard formulation for authorised force — and **fired nothing into Iran**. Six months, repeated strikes on four Gulf states plus Jordan and Iraq, condemnations from every host government and **zero Gulf munitions fired into Iran**. |
| “The Hormuz closure would either resolve or be priced as temporary by the shipping industry” | **The world's largest tanker operator withdrew its resumption timeline entirely.** **Mitsui O.S.K. Lines** CEO **Jotaro Tamura**: *“Given the current situation, it's difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year,”* abandoning a prior assumption of **phased resumption from October** and **normal operations from January**, with **no plan to return** absent **guarantees and evidence of sustainably safe passage**. **The party bearing the hull risk is now more pessimistic than the prediction markets, which price December 31 reopening at 27%, down from 28%.** |
| “China is insulated from the American campaign in the Gulf” | **Its refiners lost a third of their Iranian barrels in a month.** Preliminary **Kpler** figures put Chinese imports of Iranian crude at **~534,000 bpd in August** against **~823,000 bpd in July** and a **1.4m bpd** average last year, with **September and October offers collapsed** and **Shandong teapots** substituting **Russian Urals and fuel oil** because **ESPO sold out weeks ago**; **throughput cuts are expected in October**. **The blockade achieved what fourteen sanctions packages did not, without a single American designation of a Chinese entity — three weeks before the September 24 summit.** |
| “Venezuelan oil will offset the Hormuz disruption” | **Not this decade.** *The National* reports the **~$100bn** American bet facing a years-long wait: extra-heavy crude requiring upgraders that **“you just cannot build in a couple of years”** (Kpler); **~1.4m bpd by 2028**; **at most 300,000 bpd of additions by 2030**; **3m bpd only by 2040**; greenfield output **not before 2033-34**. Against **Energy Secretary Chris Wright's** projection of **2m bpd by decade's end**. **The theatre that was supposed to offset Hormuz cannot do so on any timescale relevant to this war.** |
| “The oil price would move on a presidential claim to have taken over Iran” | **Brent rose 0.16%.** On **September 4** — the day the President said the United States has *“essentially taken over Iran,”* the CENTCOM commander ordered a civilian-casualty review, the Iranian Red Crescent filed with the ICC, the world's largest tanker operator withdrew from the route and an Israeli division took a fortified ridge in Lebanon — **Brent closed at $95.83, up sixteen basis points**, with Trading Economics recording **$95.23, down 0.31%**. **Predictions of $150+ crude remain disconfirmed, and the December 31 reopening probability slipped from 28% to 27%.** |
| “The reported Ukrainian hold-fire order of September 5-8 is a confirmed unilateral ceasefire” | **It is reported, not announced, and its scope is unknown.** ***Ukrainska Pravda***, citing sources in multiple brigades and a senior security official, reports the order; **no Ukrainian authority has acknowledged it**, and whether it covers defensive fire, artillery, drone operations or all sectors has not been established. **Zelensky's public pledge covers airstrikes only.** **Russia has not responded, and struck the SBU headquarters in central Kyiv in daylight hours before the offer was made.** Carried as **contested_unresolved**; the cleanest discriminator — whether the pause is extended, made conditional, or lapses on September 8 regardless of outcome — resolves within days. |
| “A government that has named the fall of the Iranian state as its war aim is building the force to accomplish it” | **It capped the force and lengthened the tours.** On the same days that **Netanyahu** named toppling the Iranian regime as Israel's **“central mission”** and **Trump** asked when Iranians would **“rise up and fight,”** the *Wall Street Journal* reported Secretary **Hegseth** extending Middle East deployments **into 2027** while **holding** the force at **50,000 troops and 19 warships** *“in part to give the president flexibility on next steps,”* with Army air-defence tours grown **from nine months to twelve**. **No new brigades, no new amphibious lift, no mobilisation, no call-up, and no objective on Iranian soil named anywhere in the reporting.** |
| “Faced with a second night of Iranian strikes on four countries, the United States would escalate on the ground” | **It boarded two merchant ships.** CENTCOM's ledger moved to **87 vessels redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded** for **“total compliance”** — armed American personnel on a merchant deck in international water. **That is the highest rung of physical intrusion recorded in 190 days, and it stands against zero landings, zero raids and zero seizures of territory.** |
| “The uniformed military's objection to a prolonged Iran war would be answered on the merits” | **It was removed from the network instead.** *The Washington Post* reported on **September 2** that the Pentagon pulled decades of **Secretary of Defense Orders Book** material from **SIPRNet** after the Post published flag officers' **August 14** warning that **“a prolonged, large-scale conflict against Iran is unsustainable.”** Spokesman **Sean Parnell** declined to discuss it and **did not deny it**. **The judgement stands unreversed; the record of it is no longer visible from outside the building.** |
| “Support for the war would rise as the campaign intensified” | **31% support it and roughly 63% oppose it.** *Reuters/Ipsos*, late August 2026, with voters specifically unhappy about fuel prices. *Reuters* reports senior aides pushing to keep the war from escalating **until after the November 3 midterms** to limit Republican losses. **The constraint on American escalation is now domestic and dated.** |
| “The oil price would move on a declared war aim of regime collapse” | **Brent rose 0.60%.** On **September 3** — the day the Israeli Prime Minister named the fall of the Iranian government as Israel's central mission, the American President echoed it, Iran struck four countries for a second night, and Lloyd's List disclosed **$2bn in war-risk claims** — **Brent closed at $95.87, up sixty basis points.** **Predictions of $150+ crude remain disconfirmed, and the mechanism is now published: $7-8 of the barrel is war-risk insurance, not scarcity.** |
| “Iran could convert control of the Strait into transit revenue” | **Oman refused, including the voluntary version.** A senior regional official told the *New York Post* that Muscat rejected Iran's joint fee scheme outright to avoid a quarrel with President Trump, who threatened on **August 17** to *“bomb the hell out of”* the sultanate. Foreign Minister **Sayyid Badr** calls transit fees **“internationally prohibited.”** **The IRGC had claimed a deal was reached. There is no deal, and no littoral partner will legitimate one.** |
| “Seizing Kharg Island is required to stop Iranian oil exports” | **Kharg is draining without an American on it.** *Kpler* puts **Iranian loadings at 251,000 bpd in August 2026** with **oil stocks at Kharg down 550,000 barrels to 19.45 million**, against roughly **30 million barrels** of storage capacity; **Kharg handles 94% of Iranian crude exports**. **Operations halted July 31. The island has never been landed on, and its oil infrastructure has never been struck.** |
| “Army Secretary Dan Driscoll's resignation took effect on September 3” | **This reference's own claim, and it is now contested.** *The Washington Post* reported on **September 3** that **President Trump suggested Driscoll could remain through the midterms**, with Driscoll voicing concerns about the damage Secretary Hegseth is doing to the Army and the **White House disputing that characterisation**. **The post is carried as contested rather than vacant.** The underlying signal is unchanged on either reading: an Army secretary who resigned over readiness and personnel disputes, no Senate-confirmed chief of staff, and **more than 80 flag officers fired or blocked**. |
| “The Strait of Hormuz is running at or near pre-war throughput” | **Unresolved, and the spread is an order of magnitude.** **Vance** claims **15m barrels overnight**, **Wright** claimed **>17m** on August 31, **Bessent** says flows are “nearing prewar levels,” and US officials told *CNN* the September 1-2 operation escorted **40 vessels carrying 18m barrels**. Against that: **Kpler** counted **five ships** crossing on Monday; **TankerTrackers.com** averages **~4.9m barrels a day** since mid-July; the **IMF and Oxford Economics** count **fewer than five tanker crossings a day**; and the *straits.live* board carries **six transits** against an **85/day** baseline. **Goldman Sachs** and **ISW**, the two parties with no stake in the American performance narrative, both land in the middle — **two-thirds of pre-war Gulf export volume** and **~40 transits**. **51 of 244 screened tankers went AIS-dark in 24 hours, which explains the spread without resolving it. Treat every claim of a “reopened” or “functioning” Strait as an assertion, not a fact.** |

The **31st MEU** went home with her. **There has been one amphibious ready group and one MEU in CENTCOM since July** — the **Boxer ARG** with the **11th MEU** and **BLT 3/5** — approximately **2,200-2,500 Marines**, not the ~4,700 across two units this reference carried. **The correction runs against this audit's own argument and strengthens the finding: the United States halved its amphibious presence in the sixth month of the campaign and did not replace it.** |
| “Faced with attacks on shipping, the United States would board or seize Iranian vessels” | **It put missiles into their engine rooms from drones.** On **September 1-2**, under a new **“tanker for tanker” policy approved by the President**, US drones struck **two Iranian government tankers at anchor north of the blockade line** — the first American strike on Iranian tankers framed as **retaliation** rather than blockade enforcement. **A Marine expeditionary unit was in range and was not employed.** Washington skipped the boarding rung, the seizure rung and the landing rung in a single decision. |
| “A hundred-target strike wave against a sovereign state would move the oil price” | **It moved it 0.06%.** Brent closed at **$95.32** on **September 2**, up **six basis points**, after a 4.99% session the day before — through a **~100-target American wave across four Iranian provinces**, a **new named maritime doctrine**, the **first Saudi attribution of an attack to Iran in the war**, **two dead seafarers**, and **Secretary Rubio's foreclosure of the June memorandum**. **The market has priced this war's ceiling.** |
| “The Trump administration's energy statistics can be taken as a factual baseline” | **Contested on the record by a named commercial tracker, and the underlying series then collapsed.** Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** claimed **>17m barrels** through Hormuz on **August 31** and regional exports **above pre-war levels**. **TankerTrackers.com**'s **Samir Madani** called it *“mathemagics,”* identifying **multi-day ship-to-ship transfers aggregated into one day**, and put the real figure at **~9.14m** — against a **28-day average of 6.85m** and a **pre-war baseline of ~15m through Hormuz alone**. Volumes then fell to **6.81m on September 1** and **4.63m on September 2**. **This reference records the DOE figure as an official claim and the TankerTrackers series as the operating estimate; the two are not reconcilable.** |

Not one host state has announced any change to American basing.** This is three days after the Supreme Leader asked Gulf rulers to *“identify your real enemy.”* |

In **Khuzestan**, **7 killed and 8 injured**. |

CENTCOM has named **only military target categories** and **no installation**; Iran has published **no production loss**. **This reference no longer treats the August 1 cancellation as operative merely because it has not been publicly rescinded, and does not upgrade the energy-strike predictions on a target-city list alone.** Logged as open. |
| “American escalation against Iran is bounded only by political will” (reaffirmed and hardened) | **Bounded by an officer corps being removed at a tenth.** A *New York Times* analysis finds Secretary **Hegseth has fired or blocked the promotions of more than 80 generals and admirals — about 10% of the military's top officers** — with **six to seven more two-star selectees blocked on September 2**. **Army Secretary Driscoll's resignation takes effect September 3**, leaving the Army with **neither a Senate-confirmed secretary nor a Senate-confirmed chief of staff**. Its deployed brigade combat team is on a **twelve-month tour**; its allocation is **capped at 50,000** over **four formal four-star non-concurs**; and **its amphibious lift in theatre has halved since July**. |

| “A Trump-brokered settlement would end the Russia-Ukraine war in 2026” | **The structure Putin will accept is the one Kyiv has refused.** On **September 2** Putin pledged to continue the war, claimed Russia is winning, and said he **will not negotiate with Ukrainian “terrorists”** — while saying he is **comfortable dealing with President Trump's special envoys**. A settlement negotiated bilaterally over Kyiv's head is the arrangement Ukraine has rejected since 2025. **Witkoff and Kushner remain expected in Moscow and Kyiv; no ceasefire, no air truce and no agreed round exists.** |

COSCO's standing listing — the Pentagon's Chinese-military-companies list, **January 2025** — carries **procurement bans and no sanctions** and was **not altered**. The same Treasury is running **weekly rolling secondary sanctions against Iranian banks and airline lessors**. **The operative variable is not the severity of the conduct but whether a summit is pending: Trump and Xi meet in Washington later this month.** |

Beijing's response was foreign ministry spokesman **Guo Jiakun**: *“China's legitimate rights and interests in Venezuela must be guaranteed.”* **No sanction, no arbitration, no retaliation** — while the American energy secretary said publicly that **China will have no claim on the revenue**. |

The automatic-registration rulemaking, submitted **March 30** and **withdrawn July 23, 2026**, **has still not been re-proposed**. **No call-up, no mobilisation order, no Presidential Reserve Call-up, no IRR activation.** In 189 days the manpower pressure of this war has produced a **twelve-month tour extension**, the **resignation of the Army Secretary**, and the **removal or blocking of more than 80 flag officers** — the signatures of a force being stretched and thinned, not expanded. |
| “An escalating air campaign against Iran's littoral is the shaping phase of an amphibious operation” | **Falsified by the striking command's own published target list.** On **September 1** CENTCOM struck **five coastal locations** — Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Sirik, Konarak, Chabahar — and named what it hit: **air defence sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites**. Every category is a sensor, an emitter, a launcher or a node; **not one is terrain that must be occupied to be denied**. Shaping fires for a landing concentrate on one objective, persist, and are followed by movement. These dispersed across five locations in a single wave, two Marine Expeditionary Units within a day's steaming were not employed, and **nothing moved**. **Day 188 with zero US ground troops inside Iran.** |
| “American escalation against Iran is bounded only by political will” | **Bounded by the Army as an institution, documented from inside it.** As of **September 3, 2026** the United States Army has **neither a Senate-confirmed civilian secretary nor a Senate-confirmed military chief**: Secretary **Dan Driscoll** resigned on **August 31** after disputes with Secretary Hegseth over transformation, readiness and a promotion list, and Hegseth had already asked the chief of staff to step down. Its deployed brigade combat team is on a **twelve-month tour** for want of replacements; its allocation is **capped at 50,000** by the August 14 Orders Book over **four formal four-star non-concurs**; and the **Chief of Naval Operations** has told the Secretary of Defense the Navy *“cannot sustain its current level of support.”* |
| “The United States asserted the IRGC struck the tankers, so the IRGC struck the tankers” | **An assertion is not an attribution.** Both supertankers hit off **Khasab** on **August 31** — the **Sidr** and the **Senegal Prosperity** — were struck by projectiles that **Marisks, Kpler, UKMTO and Bloomberg all describe as “unknown,”** and **no party has claimed responsibility**. No imagery, track data, debris analysis or intercept tying the munitions to the IRGC has been published. Iran, which claimed its Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain operations openly and by name in the same week, has not admitted these. The audit records the attacks as documented and the attribution as **contested and unresolved** (`khasab-tanker-attacks-attribution-september-2026`) — declining both to endorse the American assertion and to treat missing evidence as disproof. |
| “Iranian retaliation against Gulf and Levantine basing would produce mass American casualties” | **Across the August 31 and September 1 exchanges — five bases in four countries — the confirmed casualty total from Iranian fire is zero.** Jordan intercepted **10 of 13** missiles with three falling in remote areas and no casualties; Kuwait and Bahrain reported clean air-defence engagements with no injuries or damage; **US officials reported no American casualties**. The IRGC's claim of *“a large number”* of US personnel killed at Camp Titin is unconfirmed and contradicted by US reports. **The confirmed casualties of the cycle are Iranian civilians at a wedding in Kuhestak.** |
| “Iran's outreach to the Gulf monarchies would produce a realignment against the United States” | **Foreclosed for this phase by Iran itself.** On **August 30** the Supreme Leader asked Gulf rulers to *“identify your real enemy”* and build mutual defence with Iran. On **September 1**, seventy-two hours later, Iranian military spokesman **Ebrahim Zolfaghari** said Iran *“will no longer exercise restraint regarding Bahrain and Kuwait”* and that *“gifts are on the way.”* Four hosts absorbed Iranian fire in a single night and **none announced any change to American basing**; none condemned the US strikes; Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Oman issued no statement at all. |

The pattern established by Poland's declination in late July now holds across multiple members and multiple incidents. **The corpus's model of automatic alliance escalation on airspace violation is disconfirmed as a mechanism, not merely as an outcome.** |

Samuel Paparo** filed a formal non-concur against the stripping of his theatre. On **September 1** Washington accused **COSCO** of running fleet-wide signals intelligence against the American homeland — and imposed **no sanction, no designation and no port restriction** — while both governments confirmed a **Trump–Xi summit in Washington later this month**. No PLA action against Taiwan. |
| “China would take Venezuela's oil” (mechanism update) | **Not merely absent — reversed.** Reuters reports on **September 1** that the fields **North American Blue Energy Partners** is taking over under the 100-year concession were **previously operated by Chinese and Russian firms**. The transaction is a **displacement of Beijing and Moscow from Venezuelan production**, with the **US Defense Department taking 35% equity** and the **State Department a right to 20% of output at cost**. |
| “The US government holds 55% of the Venezuelan oil joint venture” | **This reference's own figure, and it conflated two different instruments.** The September 1 White House disclosure gives the structure: the **Defense Department takes a 35% equity stake** in a joint-venture company with NABEP, and the **State Department takes a right to purchase 20% of NABEP's output at the cost of production**, plus a **right of first refusal** on the remainder. **Equity is ownership; an offtake right at cost is a purchase option.** The corrected record is 35% DoD equity plus a 20% State offtake right — not a single 55% government holding. |
| “The Strait of Hormuz crisis would push oil above $150/bbl” | **Disconfirmed at 188 days and through the sharpest escalation of the war.** Brent's wartime peak was approximately **$120.88**; on **September 1**, with the Strait effectively closed, a five-location American strike campaign under way, two supertankers hit and Russia's Ust-Luga terminal burning, Brent closed at **$95.29**. The mechanism is established: OPEC spare capacity, SPR releases, demand destruction, and roughly **15–16m bpd** still leaving the Gulf against a pre-conflict 22–24m. |
| “Stopping Iranian oil exports requires seizing Kharg Island” (reaffirmed) | Kpler puts **Kharg loadings at 135,000 bpd in August 2026** against **1.98m bpd in February** — a **93% collapse** produced by naval blockade with **no American on the island** and no strike on its oil infrastructure. On **September 1** the President renewed the Kharg threat and again raised **taking control** of Iranian energy infrastructure — which is the live counter-indicator, since a destroyed terminal is not a captured one, and is why this reference does not treat the open-ended Kharg predictions as dead. |
| "The war has effectively lifted sanctions on Iran and let it earn more from oil than it spends on its military" | Falsified in both directions and re-scored **disconfirmed** on September 1. **Kharg loadings fell to 135,000 bpd in August 2026 against 1.98m bpd in February — a 93% collapse** — with satellite imagery showing all three berths empty after operations halted on **July 31**. CENTCOM's **Adm. Brad Cooper** (August 28): *"No ships have entered or left an Iranian port without our permission."* Sanctions were **escalated**, not lifted: Treasury's **"Operation Economic Outcast,"** Bessent's **"financial violence"** formulation, three packages in August, and reported EU backing **"in the strongest terms."** The only surviving element is narrow: **no Chinese institution has been designated across three consecutive packages**, which the AP reported as deliberate signalling of reluctance to penalise major trading partners. Selective enforcement against third parties is not sanctions relief for Iran. |
| "The President said Kharg Island was destroyed, so Kharg Island was struck" | **A claimed strike is not a strike.** Trump's **August 31** Truth Social post — an **AI-generated video** captioned **"Kharg Island being blown to smithereens!!!"** — was contradicted within hours by **a US official**, who said no such attack had occurred and Kharg was not among the overnight targets; **CENTCOM's own statement** named only Larak. NIOC chief executive **Hamid Bovard** called it **"laughable"** and reported operations **"calm and appropriate."** No US strike on Kharg's export infrastructure appears anywhere in the official record of the war. |
| "China would take Venezuela's oil under a US-China grand bargain" | Re-scored **disconfirmed** on September 1. On **August 28, 2026** Venezuela granted a **100-year concession** over fields holding **65 billion barrels** — about **21% of the country's 303 billion** — to a joint venture in which the **United States government holds 55%**, secured *"at no cost to the American taxpayer."* The counterparty is Washington, not Beijing; **no Chinese investment or modernisation agreement has been announced at any point**; and the US-China grand bargain the prediction depended on never materialised. |
| "Iranian oil revenue would rise as the war loosened enforcement" | The blockade is the enforcement. Iranian crude exports are running at roughly **7% of their pre-war level**, the President is threatening secondary sanctions on third countries, and Treasury has stood up a named financial campaign against Iran's payment channels. What has loosened is enforcement **against China and India**, not against Iran. |
| "No brigade combat team, division headquarters or corps-level enabler set has been in theatre at any point in the war" | **This audit's own claim, and it was wrong.** The **82nd Airborne** extension published on **August 31** disclosed that the Army element deployed to CENTCOM in **March 2026** comprises a **Division Headquarters**, the **1st Brigade Combat Team**, the **Combat Aviation Brigade**, **DIVARTY**, the **307th Division Engineer Battalion**, **3-4 Air Defense Artillery** and a sustainment element — **approximately 2,000 soldiers**, not the ~1,000 loose paratroopers this reference carried. A division headquarters and a brigade combat team with organic artillery, engineers, air defence, aviation and sustainment have been in theatre for five months. The correction is to the record, not to the disposition: no unit moved in this cycle, none has been reinforced or tasked, and all of it has now been **frozen in place for twelve months** rather than employed. |
| "A tour extension is evidence of a build-up toward an operation" | The **82nd Airborne** extension **adds no soldiers, moves nobody forward and assigns no mission**. The **August 14 Secretary of Defense Orders Book** directs that the 50,000 figure be **held**, not raised, and the reason is in the same document: the **Chief of Naval Operations** told the Secretary of Defense the Navy **"cannot sustain its current level of support"** with **barely a quarter of the destroyer fleet ready to deploy**. Extending tours to twelve months is what a volunteer force does when it has **no replacements** — the inverse of a concentration signature. |
| "American escalation options in the Gulf are constrained only by political will" | The **August 14 Orders Book** records **four formal non-concurs** — the **Chief of Naval Operations** and the commanders of **INDOPACOM, EUCOM and SOUTHCOM** — against sustaining the **current** commitment, let alone enlarging it. More than **half** the cruise-missile and advanced air-defence-missile inventories are expended; **~25% of the Reaper fleet** is gone; **THAAD** has been pulled off the **Korean peninsula** and a carrier out of the **Pacific**; three geographic combatant commands say their homeland-defence obligations are already degraded. The collective position was recorded as **"We will carry out the orders, but at a price."** |
| "Stopping Iranian oil exports requires seizing Kharg Island" | Kpler puts **Kharg loadings at 135,000 bpd in August 2026** against **1.98m bpd in February** — a **93% collapse** produced by naval blockade with **no American on the island**. The instrument the prediction says is necessary has been shown unnecessary for the objective the prediction assigns it. |
| "China would exploit the window created by American commitment in the Gulf" | The window is now documented from the **American** side and Beijing still has not moved. The **August 14 Orders Book** records **INDOPACOM's Adm. Samuel Paparo** formally objecting to the stripping of his theatre, the **Pacific without carrier coverage**, and **THAAD removed from Korea**. US reconnaissance sorties in the South China Sea remain **down ~30%** since the war began. If the window theory were right, this was the week. |
| "Iranian retaliation escalates the conflict a rung with each exchange" | Iran ran a **named two-country operation** — *"Punishment of the Aggressor"* — against American basing in **Jordan** and claimed one in the **UAE**, and produced **zero casualties**. It did not attack shipping in the Strait, did not strike Saudi or Qatari facilities, and did not strike Israel. The American answer was a **televised threat with no accompanying sortie** in the following twenty-four hours. |
| "The Treasury's escalatory rhetoric reflects an unchanged maximal war aim" | The Treasury Secretary said on **August 31** that Iran could feel the effects *"within weeks or months — **and the economy doesn't have to collapse**."* The same official had said the campaign would *"collapse this regime."* |
| "Host-nation basing becomes politically unsustainable when it draws attacks" | **Jordan** and the **UAE** each responded to strikes on American-used facilities on their own soil by **publicly minimising the damage** — eight missiles intercepted with no injuries, one drone intercepted offshore, reports of strikes on Al Menhad declared **"false"** — rather than by questioning the presence that attracted them. Neither **Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar** nor **Oman** commented at all. |
| "Northeast Asian alliance management is insulated from Middle East policy" | The President has publicly tied his reduction of **Ulchi Freedom Shield** — cut from eleven days to five, its counteroffensive phase never conducted, a further exercise cancelled — to **Seoul's refusal to join US action against Iran**, and the **August 14 Orders Book** records **THAAD physically redeployed from South Korea** to the Middle East. |
| "The absence of a US landing in Iran only proves the occasion never arose" | The occasion arose on **August 30** and the answer was aircraft. IRGC launchers on **Larak Island** — a small island inside the Strait, not a defended mainland objective — were preparing to fire rockets carrying **sea mines** into the waterway, **five days after** the President staked his credibility on a **"Zero Tolerance"** anti-mining rule and **two days after** his theatre commander declared the lanes clear. Destroying launchers and denying a small island is the **textbook mission of an embarked Marine Expeditionary Unit**, and the **11th MEU's 2,200-2,500 Marines** were embarked and untasked in the Arabian Sea a day's steaming away. The United States **destroyed two launchers from the air and put nobody ashore**. This converts a disconfirmation argued from 185 days of absence into one argued from **conduct under maximum pressure**. |
| "The pause in US strikes on Iran was a durable strategic pivot to economic pressure" | It lasted **twenty-nine nights** and ended on **August 30**, within **five days** of the mine-clearing declaration and within days of the *Axios*-reported assurance that Secretary **Rubio** had told allied foreign ministers no new strikes were expected *"for the time being,"* with a second official saying the posture would hold **until after the midterms**. The audit logged the pause as a **pause** throughout and declined to score it as a termination. What August 30 does **not** settle is whether the campaign has **resumed**: one strike on two launchers, with an imminent-threat predicate matching a rule announced five days earlier, is compatible with enforcement and with a first night. Logged as `larak-strike-enforcement-or-campaign-resumption-august-2026`. |
| "Adversarial convergence on a number is evidence the number is right" | On Iranian oil exports, **Washington and Tehran agree and the disinterested measurement disagrees with both**. CENTCOM says exports have been **zero** since mid-July; Iran's own **central bank governor** said the same on **August 20**. **Kpler** records approximately **260,000 bpd loaded** at Iranian ports in August — down **more than 80%** on August 2025 and **~70%** on July, but not zero. Each government has an independent reason to prefer zero: Washington to validate the instrument it chose over a ground campaign, Tehran to justify emergency economic measures and to price its conditions for reopening the Strait. Convergence between adversaries carries **little evidentiary weight when both benefit from the same figure**. See `iran-oil-exports-zero-or-loading-august-2026`. |
| "Escalatory rhetoric from the Treasury indicates escalatory action against China" | The Treasury Secretary reached his strongest verbal position of the war — *"financial violence,"* *"all options are on the table,"* and a denial of any reluctance as *"a completely false narrative that the media picked up on"* — in the same interview in which the action described was against **an Egyptian bank's Emirati branches**. **No Chinese financial institution has been designated in three consecutive packages.** Independent reporting now treats the gap as the story: *Fortune* found the world **"mostly shrugged off"** the threat and a former Treasury official said the actions *"do not match the hype."* The structural reason is stated plainly: an effective campaign requires sanctioning China, which risks a global shock; not doing so leaves insufficient pressure on Iran. |
| "Declaring the Strait de-mined would settle the mining question" | It survived **five days**. On **August 25** the President declared all mines disposed of in the Strait's international waters and all **28 Iranian mine-laying boats** destroyed; on **August 28** Admiral Cooper declared the lanes free of Iranian sea mines and called it a **"major milestone"**; on **August 30** US forces struck **launchers preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the same waterway**. The demining claim survives on its own terms — what was struck was the **means of re-mining**, not a laid minefield — which is precisely why the audit logged the demining claim and the residual-threat question separately. Ambrey's **Alex Almeida** stands confirmed that mines *"have never been the primary threat."* |
| "A resumption of US strikes would open the ground rung" | The strike resumed **on the air rung and nowhere else**. The theatre commander's own description of his force is naval and air — *"around 50,000 US troops are executing a blockade,"* more than **20 warships**, **hundreds of aircraft**, the only ground personnel named being **Navy divers and SEALs** clearing mines and the only Marine Corps contribution named being **air power**. The **Boxer ARG remains split across two oceans**, with **USS Comstock** — the dock landing ship that lands vehicles and heavy equipment — in the **Indian Ocean**. Iran's answer was **missiles at Jordan**, nearly all intercepted. **No landing, no lodgement, no Kharg action, no reinforcement, no mobilisation, no draft order.** |
| "Belligerents do not announce their strike campaigns in advance" | Russia did, on **August 30**: its Defence Ministry said the armed forces *"have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure"* in retaliation for Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries — weeks before the heating season and against a target set that can be defended. **Pre-announcement forfeits surprise for no operational gain**, which is exactly what makes the statement legible as a **conditional threat** as well as a warning order. The audit records it as a **stated intention, not an executed act**, so that a campaign that follows is scored as an escalation when it occurs and a campaign that never comes is not quietly dropped. |
| "Iran's supreme leader is absent because he has been sidelined" | Reuters reported on **August 30** that **Mojtaba Khamenei** has not been seen in public **because he was injured in the February 28 US-Israeli airstrikes** that killed his father. It is the first published explanation for an absence this audit has logged for six months, and it is physical rather than political. In the same 48 hours he issued **two substantive written directives** — a Government Week economic programme and an Islamic Unity Week appeal to Gulf rulers — and the government is executing against both. **Incapacity of the person is not paralysis of the system.** |
| "Bearing the cost of the closure would push affected states behind the US sanctions regime" | It has not. **Pakistan**, whose power prices rose **4.25%** in April and which has joined **more than 32 nations** calling for resolution, says it *"is not obliged"* to respond to unilateral sanctions and continues overland trade. **India** and **China** sit inside the same **30-plus state** coalition formed around energy costs — a grouping that spans the US-China divide. The **UAE** declares a rupture with Iran while **Iranian bank branches stay open in Dubai**. **Turkey** has received no formal guidance and keeps flying. The compliance being obtained is **declaratory**. |
| "The open-versus-closed dispute over Hormuz would be settled by the transit data" | The transit data does not discriminate. **114 transits August 17-27**, up **more than 30%** on the week, arrived in the same cycle in which Iran asserted that *"any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran."* A 30% weekly rise with **no change in the declared closure** is compatible with an improving American escort regime **and** with an Iranian permissioning arrangement; escorted and de-conflicted convoys produce identical AIS signatures. Six months of framing the question as open-versus-closed may have been the wrong question. |
| "The Iran-Oman corridor would represent a reopening of the Strait" | On Iran's own published description it would **close** the UN-authorised **southern route** along Oman's coast **and** the temporary northern route near Larak Island, replacing both with a **single seven-mile corridor entered — and partly exited — through Iranian territorial waters**. That is a change in the **legal character** of transit through Hormuz, not a restoration of the pre-war regime. The arrangement also remains **suspended** behind an American precondition Washington has not met. |
| "Marines published in theatre would signal an imminent landing" | The first CENTCOM-published imagery of Marine ground personnel in this theatre in weeks shows them **refuelling an MV-22 Osprey** — the most routine task an expeditionary unit performs — and it was **published rather than concealed**. In the same cycle the **Boxer ARG dispersed**, with **USS Comstock**, the dock landing ship that lands vehicles and heavy equipment, moving into the **Indian Ocean** while Boxer stayed in the Arabian Sea. The tell for a landing is concentration and silence; both moved the other way. |
| "A ground campaign would be preceded by domestic political preparation for casualties" | The scheduled American action of the cycle was a **September 1 pricing meeting with oil refiners** — Valero, Marathon and PBF — about gasoline above **$4/gal** ahead of November midterms. That is an administration optimising for the domestic cost of a **sustained blockade**, not preparing a public for a ground war. |
| "A draft would follow if the war ran long" | At six months the binding constraint is **munitions, not manpower**. Troop strength in CENTCOM has been **flat at ~50,000 since July** — reaffirmed August 28 — while roughly **half the Patriot inventory** and **two-thirds of the THAAD stockpile** have been expended against two-year replacement times. **Conscription does not manufacture interceptors.** The only Selective Service change of record remains the **administrative automatic-registration rule due December 18, 2026**, which registers and does not conscript. |
| "Chinese banks would be sanctioned once the financial campaign matured" | For the **second consecutive package** they were not, and the campaign's geography is now articulated: *Iran International*'s analysis of the Banque Misr action found it aimed at **Dubai, Istanbul and Baghdad** — **not Beijing**. The instrument fired, a FinCEN correspondent-banking rule, is precisely the one that would be used against a Chinese institution; it was demonstrated on a target with **no capacity to retaliate**. |
| "China would open a Taiwan front while America was committed in the Middle East" | **PLA fighter sorties near Taiwan fell to a three-year low in the first half of 2026** — below the pre-Lai baseline — during the deepest US commitment to the Middle East in a generation. Late-August tracking recorded **7 PLAN ships and 7 official ships** around the island. US intelligence assesses that **Russia** reads the Iran war as American weakness; **no equivalent assessment of Chinese opportunism has been published**. |
| "Deep strategic reserves would shield Japan and South Korea from the Hormuz shock" | They shielded them from **shortage**, not from **loss**. With **254** and **208 days** of cover respectively, neither faced physical scarcity — and the **Kospi fell 12%** and the **Nikkei 225 8.6%**. Reserves insulate against volume risk; they do not insulate against price risk. |
| "Civilian casualty totals index deliberate targeting" | The year's deadliest attack in Ukraine resists that reading. At **Myla** on **August 28**, **37 died** — but both belligerents agree **munitions were stored at the site** and that **secondary detonation drove the toll**. Ukrainian prosecutors described *"explosive objects"*; Russia described drone components and launch boosters. What the site was, whether it was a licit military object, and why it sat beside a care home cannot be established from open sources, and the site has been destroyed. The audit assigns the event to **neither ledger**. |
| "The Iran war would be over in four to five weeks" | It reached **six months on August 28, 2026**. The forecast was the President's own, made on **February 29**, the day after he launched the war. At six months, reporting across outlets found that **none of the six objectives** he stated at the launch has been fully achieved, Iran retains its enriched-uranium stockpile and the knowledge to rebuild, and Senator **Jack Reed** characterised the campaign as a **"policy failure of historic consequence."** (*The Washington Post*; *ms.now*; Associated Press, August 28, 2026.) |
| "American ground forces would enter Iran once air power reached its limits" | At the six-month mark the **President himself** described the war as one **"in which no American troops have deployed into Iran."** It is the first affirmative statement of the negative by the commander-in-chief in 184 days, and it is offered as a **defence of the campaign's design** rather than as a denial extracted under questioning. (*Fortune*, August 28, 2026.) |
| "Exhausting the air and naval campaign would open the ground rung" | The published inventory figures cut the other way. Six months of war has expended roughly **half the Patriot interceptor inventory**, **two-thirds of the THAAD stockpile** and **a third of the Tomahawks**, against **two-year replacement lead times**, with European stocks described by a US defence official as **"beyond critical."** An amphibious lodgement is the **most air- and missile-defence-intensive** option on the escalation ladder, and the covering force is the one that has been drawn down. Compounding it, Iranian strikes damaged the **Bahrain** naval supply hub and pushed sustainment onto **Diego Garcia**, lengthening rather than shortening the logistics chain — the **inverse** of the accumulation that precedes a landing. (*ABC News*; Associated Press, August 27-28, 2026.) |
| "Economic pressure alone would force Iranian capitulation inside six months" | The six-month mark passed with Tehran **issuing conditions rather than accepting terms**. **Mohsen Rezaei** said Iran is drawing up a list of demands and that **"the US must first take practical steps."** The Iranian economy is severely damaged — **66% inflation**, foreign trade **down 35%**, a **15-million-litre daily fuel deficit**, the rial above **2 million** — and the government has not moved its price across four mediators in five days. A provincial fuel-price pilot in **Kerman** was abandoned within hours for fear of 2019-style protests, which is a measure of internal fragility and also of the government's continuing capacity to act on it. (Reuters via *NBC News*; *ProtoThema English*; Associated Press, August 27-28, 2026.) |
| "The costs of the blockade would fall on Iran and its customers rather than on the United States" | The published American costs at six months: **$37.5 billion** officially with internal estimates reported at **$80-100 billion**; **18 dead and 757 wounded**; roughly **half the Patriot inventory** and **two-thirds of the THAAD stockpile** expended with two-year replacement times; the **Strategic Petroleum Reserve at 290 million barrels — 41% of capacity and the lowest since 1982**; gasoline at **$4.090** in what is on course to be the **highest August on record**; and a presidential approval rating of **33%** with midterms in November. (*Al Jazeera*; AAA, August 28, 2026.) |
| "Secondary sanctions would be applied to China's banks once the campaign escalated" | For the **second consecutive package** they were not. The **August 28** FinCEN action severed the **UAE branches of an Egyptian bank** from correspondent banking; reporting attributed the decision to stop short of full sanctions to **reluctance to penalise major trading partners including China and India**, and Bessent's stated position is that countries should have the opportunity to shift away from Iran before facing consequences. Asked directly why he had not sanctioned Chinese banks, Trump replied: *"Who said I'm not? You don't know if I'm doing it. I don't have to announce everything, do I?"* — a non-answer, with no corresponding designation in Treasury material. (*Fortune*; *CNBC*; *Al-Monitor*, August 26-28, 2026.) |

The weapon was a **projectile, not a mine**, so the demining claim survives on its own terms; what fails is the inference from it. Ambrey's **Alex Almeida** had said two days earlier that mines *"have never been the primary threat."* |

The **Justice Department** is reviving **maritime prize courts** — dormant since the **Second World War**, of negligible use since **1898** — to condemn seized Iranian tankers and cargo as **US property** for sale, with **proceeds to the Treasury**, expressly to **strengthen the blockade** and **offset the cost of the conflict**. US Attorney **Aaron Reitz**: DOJ is *"now reviving"* an *"ancient body of maritime law."* **Institution-building is what a state does when it expects to be interdicting shipping for years.** |

The **USS Abraham Lincoln** left CENTCOM on **August 22** after 200+ days; the **USS George Washington** arrived in the week of **August 20** to relieve it; the **USS Theodore Roosevelt** sails from San Diego **within weeks** to relieve the George Washington in turn, on **at least seven months with crews told to plan for eight**. Net: **one carrier on station**, against **two** cited by CENTCOM in July and **three** in April. The **USS Tripoli** is in port at **Sasebo, Japan**. **Concentration precedes a landing; relief-in-place sustains a campaign.** |

Port calls: **Kuwait -86%**, **UAE -69%**, **Qatar/Iraq/Bahrain -66-68%**, **Saudi Arabia -15%**. This sits against Trump's **August 26** claim of **ten million barrels** through the strait on Tuesday, which across five hulls would require roughly **two million barrels per vessel — about six times VLCC capacity**. The register carries both figures and adjudicates neither. |

| "An intelligence-channel visit to Moscow signalled a Ukraine settlement push" | The disclosed agenda was **NATO and Iran**. **Ratcliffe** warned Russian officials against actions escalating tensions with **Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania**, and pressed Moscow to **cut military and economic support for Iran**. **Peskov** says he met **Russian intelligence representatives, not Putin**. The Ukraine channel itself remains shut: Peskov said on **August 25** there were **no plans** for talks with Witkoff or Kushner. |

Pakistan's **Asim Munir** (August 24), Oman's **Badr Albusaidi** (August 25) and Qatar's **Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani** (August 27) all carried the Hormuz file into Tehran; security chief **Mohsen Rezai** restated the same precondition to the last of them — Washington **must first lift the naval blockade, unfreeze assets and remove oil sanctions**. On the American side the White House said there are **"no talks or conversations"** scheduled. |

US officials say Navy **unmanned underwater vehicles** scanned the Traffic Separation Scheme over several months, located **more than 100 objects suspected to be mines**, and **private companies under contract** removed or detonated them; the CENTCOM operation began in **April**. On **August 25** the President declared the Strait's international waters clear and imposed a declaratory **"zero tolerance"** rule enforced by **Space Force** surveillance. No Marine went ashore, and the amphibious ready group in theatre received no tasking. |
| "Clearing the mines would restore traffic through the Strait" | It has not, at least not yet. IMF PortWatch recorded **three transits on August 23** and Reuters **two on August 24** — the fewest since early May — and **war-risk insurance did not move** from 7.5-10% of hull value against 1-3% pre-war. Ambrey's **Alex Almeida**: mines *"have never been the primary threat"*; the greater danger is **drones and anti-ship cruise and ballistic missiles**. Clearing the seabed did not clear the risk. |
| "The future governance of the Strait of Hormuz would be settled by the United States" | The first document of the war to address it was signed by Iran and Oman. The **August 25** joint statement commits the two to a **joint temporary navigational corridor**, a **joint mine-clearing project**, and continued talks toward a **permanent corridor and "the future administration of the Strait."** The IRGC says the parties have agreed **"each country's share of the strait's waters and Iran and Oman's share of its revenues."** Washington is not a party, has taken no position, and said on **August 26** that no conversations are under way with Tehran. |

BBH: *"more of a warning shot than a decisive blow."* Saxo Bank's **Ole Hansen**: the move from military confrontation to economic sanctions *"had helped calm nerves across energy markets."* |

The stated instruments in its place are **sanctions, the naval blockade and "moving ever-increasing amounts of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz."** Logged as reporting, not as an order — and the counter-formulas remain live, with Hegseth keeping strikes *"on the table"* and Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** saying the US could destroy Iranian nuclear facilities *"if necessary."* |

On the same day **Peskov** said there were **no plans** for talks with Witkoff or Kushner: *"No, there are no such plans."* The intelligence channel is open; the diplomatic one is not. |

Tracked at `hormuz-transit-volume-dispute-august-2026`. |

A sanctions package whose enforcement is deferred behind a cure period, with no country named as a secondary-sanctions target, was priced as less disruptive than the rally that preceded it. |

Of **757 US wounded across 180 days, 19 are Marines** — roughly **2.5%** — against more than 580 Army, 86 Navy and 64 Air Force. The Boxer ARG with the 11th MEU has sat in the Arabian Sea since June 30 without a single tasking, embarkation, landing rehearsal or mine-countermeasures preparation. |
