Pakistan's army chief returned to Tehran on August 24 with the framework described as still "relevant" and available as a template — which is what is said about an instrument that is no longer operative. |
| "Reducing a US-South Korea exercise means shortening it" | In this case it meant deleting its offensive half. Ulchi Freedom Shield was scheduled as an eleven-day event in two phases, with **counteroffensive operations running to August 27**; it ended on **August 21** and the counteroffensive phase never took place. The concession was therefore larger than previously recorded — and it was still dismissed by Kim Yo Jong within 24 hours and answered with about ten ballistic missiles within 48. |
| "The United States remains the principal external sponsor of Ukraine's war effort" | Not at the anniversary it was not. European leaders travelled to Kyiv for Ukraine's 35th Independence Day on August 24 and **no United States representative attended**. Britain pledged **MBDA release of classified UK component data for the SCALP missile** so Ukraine can build local assembly lines, and Norway committed **$9 billion for 2027**. A sponsor that transfers production data rather than munitions is a sponsor working around a stock constraint. |
| "The sanctions phase would be an interlude before a ground campaign" | The administration put the opposite in writing. Bessent's *Financial Times* op-ed of August 23 announces "an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary," and he told CNBC on August 20 that "if we are doing the maximum economic pressure, then that means that likely there will not be a large-scale kinetic restart." On the same weekend, one amphibious ready group was deployed worldwide against combatant-commander requests for "well north of three" pairings, and every ground-execution indicator stood at zero for a 179th day. |
| "Two US carriers arriving in CENTCOM would signal a build-up toward a ground phase" | There is no arrival to signal from. USS George H.W. Bush has been inside CENTCOM since April 23 and USS George Washington relieved USS Abraham Lincoln on August 19 — a like-for-like rotation that leaves the count at two, which is the same number CENTCOM published in July. This entry also corrects this project's own prior record, which had described net carrier presence as one. Separately, no US carrier is currently positioned in the Western Pacific, which describes the size of the force rather than intent in the Gulf. |
| "Iran's closure of the Strait is absolute and admits of no commercial regime" | Iran is legislating a commercial regime for it. On August 23 the parliamentary National Security and Foreign Policy Commission approved a service-fee article for "authorised" transiting ships covering maritime, environmental, fueling, insurance and safety services, payable in rials or another currency Iran accepts, with violators reported to face fines, detention or confiscation — while Rezaei said the same day that the Strait "is closed and will not reopen." The regime being built is priced allocation, not closure. It is also not yet law: a floor vote and Guardian Council review remain. |
| "The Iranian leadership speaks with one voice on the war" | It did not on August 23. President Pezeshkian said Iran "cannot continue with war forever" and defended the June memorandum against what reporting describes as the purported misgivings of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, saying "one day, a decision must be made to save the country from the state of 'neither war nor peace'." On the same day the Supreme National Security Council secretary threatened to stop all oil leaving the Gulf and to retaliate "in a seismic manner." Whether this is a genuine split or a division of labour is logged as unresolved; what is disconfirmed is the premise of a single public line. |
| "Routing around the Strait of Hormuz is a straightforward technical fix" | Iran named the workarounds as targets on the eve of the summit convened to build them. On August 23 Rezaei said Iran would strike the oil-shipping routes out of the Persian Gulf that serve as alternatives to the Strait if regional states join the economic war; on August 24 Macron and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met in Paris with Omani ports, doubled pipeline capacity and new rail as the headline file, and a France-Saudi ministerial task force on Middle East-Europe energy and logistics convened the same day. Substitution is being built under an explicit threat of interdiction. |
| "Published figures establish how much traffic is moving through the Strait" | They establish the opposite. For the same period the record carries CNN at 20% of the pre-war average, straits.live at one transit against a 73-a-day baseline (1%), UKMTO at about 4% of pre-conflict levels for the week to August 7, Iran International at roughly 200 transits in a week, Al Jazeera at 236 hulls across nineteen days, and an unnamed US official at 15-20 escorted transits a night carrying about ten million barrels a day — approximately half pre-war volume. The spread is roughly fifty to one. Sixty-two per cent of the traffic in the only published route analysis went dark, which defeats the counting method the low figures rely on and is unverifiable in the escort claims that produce the high ones. Logged as an open question; every quantitative corpus prediction resting on a throughput number is scored UNTESTED for the August period. |
| "A leader-level summit offer would draw Pyongyang toward diplomacy" | The offer was made and refused inside 48 hours. On August 19 Trump confirmed he expects to meet Kim Jong Un this year, and Ulchi Freedom Shield was curtailed from eleven days to five as a goodwill gesture; Kim Yo Jong dismissed the drill reduction the same day and has denied that any Trump-Kim contact occurred, and on August 20 North Korea fired about ten KN-25 short-range ballistic missiles roughly 300 kilometres into the East Sea. The package refused was not a curtailed exercise alone but a curtailed exercise plus a presidential summit offer. |
| "Import dependence on Hormuz determines domestic fuel-price outcomes" | India is the counter-case. It avoided formal fuel rationing altogether and retail fuel prices rose by only about 7% over the crisis period, against a global average of 25-30%, despite being among the most Hormuz-exposed large importers. Policy and sourcing diversification changed the result, while South Korea, Bangladesh, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Pakistan all moved to standing rationing regimes. |
| "A US claim of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz would be the prelude to, or accompanied by, physical occupation" | The claim was made and nothing was occupied. On August 22 the President said "I view the Strait of Hormuz as an American territory right now" and re-posted a map labelling it "NEW U.S. TERRITORY"; there was no landing, no seizure of Kharg or any island, no embarkation, no MEU tasking and no change in force posture. A sovereignty assertion over water carries no manpower requirement and generated no ground signature. Every execution indicator stayed at zero for a 178th consecutive day. |
| "The United States controls traffic through the Strait of Hormuz" | The first route-share dataset of the war says otherwise on the narrow question it can answer. Of 236 hulls crossing between August 1 and 19, 83 openly used Iran's prescribed northern route against three that openly used the US-backed Omani route, with 148 going dark; among 112 oil and gas vessels the split was 21 Iranian, two Omani and 89 dark. Al Jazeera's conclusion was that "the fear of offending Tehran appears to outweigh Trump's threats." Iran additionally granted a named state-level exemption to Iraqi tankers on August 22. The claim of American control remains true of interdiction — 68 vessels redirected — and unsupported as a description of whose prohibitions shippers obey. |
| "Iran's total closure of the Strait is indiscriminate and admits no exceptions" | Tehran granted a number of Iraqi oil tankers permission to transit on August 22 after repeated Baghdad requests, the first named state-level exemption of the war, while simultaneously stating through Mohsen Rezaei that "the Strait of Hormuz is closed and will not reopen." The regime being operated is selective allocation, not blanket closure — Iraq exempted, American and Israeli vessels barred outright, the UAE's ADNOC repeatedly attacked, and a preferential trade agreement finalised with Oman. |
| "The Gulf monarchies would respond to the war as a bloc" | They are not moving as one. The UAE suspended all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran on August 19; Iraq was granted a tanker exemption by Tehran on August 22; Oman finalised preferential trade terms with Iran pending parliamentary approval; Saudi Arabia travelled to Paris to negotiate routes around the chokepoint with France; and Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan signed a mutual-defence pact among themselves on August 7. No single Gulf posture, in either direction, describes the record. |
| "The reported December 2026 automatic Selective Service registration date shows the draft rung advancing" | It shows a database being built, not an army. Automatic registration under the Defense Authorization Act provision replaces self-registration with agency registration from federal databases; it inducts no one. Conscription still requires Congress to amend the Military Selective Service Act and the President to authorise inductions, neither of which has occurred, been requested or been scheduled. The Selective Service System's own automatic-registration rule remains withdrawn since July 23 and un-re-proposed, and the "Readiness Simulation" vendor window closed in August with no award announced. Reporting also disagrees on whether the date is December 18 or December 19 and on whether the cohort is 18-25 or 18-26. |
| "Scaling back US-South Korea exercises would draw Pyongyang back toward diplomacy" | The reduction was announced on August 18, dismissed by Kim Yo Jong on August 19 as leaving the drills' "provocative, aggressive nature" unchanged, and answered with about ten short-range ballistic missiles on August 20. The concession was made, refused in words and answered in ordnance inside 48 hours. |
| "American munitions and interceptor stocks are adequate to sustain two theatres" | The clearest evidence to the contrary is now a recipient state's own procurement behaviour. ISW assessed on August 21 that Ukrainian forces are domestically developing means to target Russian ballistic launchers and jet-powered drones specifically to circumvent the need for foreign materiel amid global air-defence interceptor shortages — Kyiv designing around the American pipeline rather than waiting for it. This sits alongside CSIS's finding of more than 60% of Patriot and THAAD stocks expended with three-plus years to rebuild, and the $22.9 billion seven-year Raytheon Tomahawk contract signed August 17. |
| "The reported multi-day energy campaign was merely delayed and began later in August" | It was cancelled and never began. Trump announced the cancellation by name late on August 1, citing progress toward a deal and requests from Iran and "other Middle Eastern countries." No US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory was confirmed by CENTCOM through August 19 — a twentieth consecutive night — with no new Iranian civilian casualties from strikes across the span. The open question `iran-weekend-campaign-non-start-august-2026` is retired as resolved. |
| "The expiry of the 60-day negotiating deadline would trigger a resumption of large-scale US strikes" | The window expired on August 17 with nothing signed and no resumption followed. Trump said he had "no time schedule" and was not "in a hurry." Three days later the administration announced that the war had entered a "new phase" of ECONOMIC pressure, with Treasury Secretary Bessent stating that the US likely would not restart large-scale combat operations. |
| "The next rung above the air campaign is a ground operation" | The next rung the administration actually took was financial. Vance announced a "new phase" of economic pressure as "the best way to ultimately accomplish the final objective"; Bessent promised "the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world" with details due August 24 and said large-scale combat likely would not restart. The theatre's two capability investments in this cycle — Task Force Falcon Strike's multinational one-way attack drones and a $22.9 billion seven-year Tomahawk production contract — are investments in standoff strike. Every ground execution indicator remained at zero for a 177th consecutive day. |
| "The arrival of USS George Washington represents a naval build-up ahead of escalation" | It is a like-for-like relief. USS Abraham Lincoln departed after roughly nine months and 252 days without a port call, amid reporting of serious morale strain; George Washington arrived on August 19 with one cruiser and one destroyer. Net carrier presence is unchanged at one and no second strike group was ordered. |
| "Iran's denial of export revenue would eventually force a physical seizure of Kharg Island" | The denial is being achieved without a landing. Kharg's terminals sat empty for weeks with 16-17 tankers waiting offshore, a single dark VLCC loaded on August 12 for the first time since July 18, and Chinese purchases of Iranian crude fell from 823,000 to 534,000 barrels a day. Trump described the mechanism himself on August 17: "We control it with the blockade," a "wall of steel." The island has never been seized and was not named as a target in any reporting during this period. |
| "A prolonged US-Iran war would push the Gulf monarchies toward accommodation with Tehran" | The UAE moved the other way. After detecting two Iranian ballistic missiles on the night of August 18, Abu Dhabi suspended all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran on August 19 — cutting off a partner that had supplied more than 30% of Iranian imports. The strain on the US position in the Gulf came instead from Washington, with Trump threatening to bomb Oman, the war's principal mediator. |
| "North Korea's quiet period reflects a durable shift away from provocation" | The 157-day run without a new DPRK provocation recorded through August 2 ended. North Korea fired a short-range ballistic missile on August 6, its first ballistic testing since late June, and launched again on August 12 — a projectile flying more than 700 kilometres, Pyongyang's eleventh suspected ballistic test of 2026 — timed against announced US-South Korean drills. This briefing's prior framing is corrected. |
| "Beijing would openly defy US secondary sanctions to sustain Iranian oil revenue" | Beijing rejected the pressure rhetorically while the commercial facts moved against Tehran regardless. Chinese imports of Iranian crude fell to 534,000 barrels a day in August from 823,000 in July, offers for September and October cargoes declined, independent "teapot" refiners went on alert for buyer-specific designations, and roughly 40 million barrels sit stranded in Malaysian waters. |
| "Global oil markets would price the Hormuz disruption as a supply rupture" | Brent traded between roughly $93.40 and $95.29 on August 21 — a second consecutive weekly gain above 5% and the highest since late July, but far below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130-plus a sustained US ground commitment would imply. The disruption is being absorbed through rationing, stockpile releases and demand destruction in importing states: licence-plate rationing in South Korea, 50-litre and 15-litre daily fuel caps in Indonesia and Sri Lanka, suspended fertiliser-sector gas in Pakistan, and forty lost LNG cargoes with four of five urea plants shut in Bangladesh. |
| "The reported multi-day energy campaign began over the weekend as scheduled" | It did not begin. Through the end of August 1, 2026 no US strike wave against Iranian territory was reported by any outlet, within the window the July 31 reporting itself described. Al Jazeera recorded that Trump "had not yet authorized the potential two-week operation targeting Tehran's electricity grid." The audit records the non-occurrence and declines to infer the reason: never authorised, authorised and withheld, and deferred on materiel advice are all publicly asserted and produce an identical public signature. See open question `iran-weekend-campaign-non-start-august-2026`. |
| "The escalation to strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure is the last rung before a ground phase" | The internal argument reported in place of the campaign was between two AIR options — CENTCOM's prepared two-week air campaign and some officials' preference for "a shorter, more severe salvo" to advance negotiations (ABC News). No ground element re-entered the reporting, no landing force, embarkation, MEU tasking or Kharg operation was named, and every execution indicator remained at zero for a 157th consecutive day. |
| "American air power in this war is effectively unconstrained by materiel" | CSIS estimates more than 60% of US Patriot and THAAD interceptor stocks expended, with fewer than 827 Patriots remaining from roughly 2,200 and fewer than 278 THAAD from 452; three sources told CNN the figures are close to internal government numbers; three or more years to rebuild at 183 THAAD a year and ~3.5 years contract-to-delivery. Gen. Dan Caine is reported to have warned privately about the shortages, cited as a restraint on broader strikes. |
| "The mass departure advisories are a force-flow indicator for a ground operation" | They are the inverse. A landing is preceded by inbound movement — force flow, prepositioning, medical and fuel staging, embarkation. This cycle moved American civilians OUT of at least ten countries. The advisories are a genuine escalation indicator and are logged as one; they are not a ground indicator, and no ordered departure of official personnel or dependents — the more escalatory category — was announced. |
| "Closing a chokepoint requires physically seizing it" | Hormuz transits fell 77% in a single day, from 22 vessels to five, with no US strike wave and no new Iranian declaration. The strait has been held at roughly a tenth of normal throughput by insurance pricing, AIS-dark running and 371 vessels waiting — without either side taking ground. |
| "Congressional action will halt the Iran war" | The second war powers measure in two weeks failed. The Senate voted 49-50 against discharging Sen. Gillibrand's resolution directing withdrawal of US forces absent congressional authorisation; Collins, Murkowski and Paul crossed over, and Fetterman was the only Democrat voting to block. |
| "Iranian retaliation is confined to military targets" | US intelligence assessed Iran likely responsible for coordinated cyberattacks on more than 30 Minnesota municipal water systems, with the FBI and CISA investigating incidents in at least seven states and Michigan also affected. Programmable logic controllers were the common target; no water supply was reported compromised. |
| "The Selective Service's July 23 withdrawal means the draft machinery is being wound down" | The indicator SPLIT rather than falling. The withdrawn automatic-registration rule has still not been re-proposed and remains unexplained — but the agency is simultaneously procuring a government-owned "Readiness Simulation" to wargame staffing, processing and mobilisation scenarios, with vendor submissions due August 14, 2026 and the December 19, 2026 statutory registration start unchanged. Neither fact is a draft; conscription still requires both Congress and the President. |
| "The Iran and Ukraine theatres are independent for scoring purposes" | They are coupled through a single inventory. The interceptor Ukraine lacks against ballistic missiles is Patriot; more than 60% of US Patriot and THAAD stocks were expended defending against Iran, with three-plus years to rebuild. Ukraine downed one of twenty-seven ballistic missiles on August 1 and Zelensky said interceptors have run out, three days after pressing Trump for licences to produce Patriot interceptors in Ukraine. |
| "Brent closed July at $90.24" | Restated downward. TradingEconomics carried the July 31 settle at $87.93, +$1.05 (+1.21%), with the month at +22.86% and the year at +26.21%; the straits.live board carried the same $87.93 at 22:59 UTC on August 1. The $90.24 logged in the previous cycle was an intraday print, about $2.30 above the settle. Direction and monthly magnitude are unchanged. |
| "The US wounded figure is settled at 685" | Not across accounting bases. This project's running tally carries 685 wounded and 18 killed; the Pentagon's published total after the July split into "Operation Epic Fury" and a new "Overseas Operations" category is 624 wounded and 18 killed, a figure also carried by Wikipedia's infobox and militaryspend.org. The 61-casualty gap is an accounting-basis artefact and is flagged rather than reconciled. |
| "Russia's claimed advances in northern Ukraine are real" | ISW assessed on July 31 that Russia's Northern Grouping of Forces and high military command are likely lying to the Kremlin about the extent of gains, that available battlefield evidence does not corroborate claimed advances in northern Sumy and Kharkiv oblasts, and that Ukrainian forces are counterattacking in some areas. |
| "The resumption of large-scale US strikes means the ground phase is next" | The opposite was reported. On July 31 four outlets described the coercive package intended to force Iranian capitulation and it is a **multi-day AIR campaign** against power plants, refineries, Tehran's electricity grid and dual-use bridges. **No ground element appears in any version** — no landing, embarkation, MEU tasking, airborne insertion or Kharg operation — and the Kharg-seizure option prepared since March, built around two MEUs and 1,000-2,000 soldiers of the 82nd Airborne, existed to supply exactly the leverage this air campaign is now reported to be seeking. Ground rung unchanged for a 156th day: ~50,000 personnel, Boxer ARG unmoved in the Arabian Sea, no relief ARG, no draft. |
| "Trump has ordered the multi-day campaign against Iran's energy infrastructure" | **Contested, not established.** The *Wall Street Journal* reported it as ordered; *CBS News* reported that Trump **has not given final authorisation** and the plan remains pending his decision; *CNN*'s two officials said it **could be called off**; *Axios* reported it as under consideration; and an Israeli official said Israel is **"unaware of a decision."** The project records the reporting and scores on execution. |
| "Israel has been enlisted for the coming energy campaign" | Denied on the Israeli record. An Israeli official said: "Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations, nor has been requested of Israel to join any military actions against Iran" — against multiple US sources telling CBS that Israel had been notified and was coordinating. |
| "Iran's promised retaliation for the July 30 wave never materialised" | It materialised the next day, by drone, across three countries. Iran's army and the IRGC claimed one-way attack drone strikes on US facilities at Sheikh Isa (Bahrain), Ahmad al-Jaber and Ali al-Salem (Kuwait) and Al Azraq (Jordan), with specific target descriptions and a claim of "significant damage." No US or host-nation comment followed and no casualties were reported. |
| "Iran carried out the Damietta attack on Egypt" | **Not established, and now denied on two sides.** Araghchi denied Iranian involvement, called Egypt "an important friend and partner in the region" and alleged an Israeli false flag; Egypt's Diaa Rashwan publicly dismissed a *WSJ* report that Cairo believed Iran responsible; drone debris is under forensic analysis; no party has claimed responsibility; and Trump's July 30 attribution was made without published evidence. |
| "The July 30 Hormuz 'reopening' readings were real" | They were not. The straits.live board reverted on July 31 to its prior framing — latest recorded volume of 10 transits against an 88/day pre-crisis baseline, or **11% of normal throughput** — confirming the previous cycle's assessment that the 35-transit/1,357-stranded print reflected a zone-definition change rather than a surge. Independent S&P Global data show the real movement: 28 transits on July 29, a two-week high, on resumed LNG traffic. |
| "Washington leads the naval coalitions in this war" | Not in the Red Sea, and not yet in the Gulf. **Saudi Arabia** convened military representatives of **43 countries** in Riyadh on July 30 for a maritime defence coalition it would **headquarter**, drawing thirteen public backers — in the same week Britain and France continued to refuse to co-lead Hegseth's Hormuz escort coalition absent an enduring ceasefire. |
| "The July 28 US-Saudi strikes in Iraq were coordinated with Baghdad, as Trump said" | **Baghdad says they were not.** On July 31 the Iraqi government stated it had no prior knowledge of the strikes, directly contradicting the President; its National Security Council had already called them "a flagrant violation of Iraq's sovereignty," and Baghdad suspended PM al-Zaidi's planned visit to Saudi Arabia. Neither government has published a notification record. |
| "A Russian missile detonating inside NATO territory triggers an Article 5 process" | It did not, again. A projectile assessed as a Kh-101 exploded near Tarnawa-Kolonia outside Lublin on July 30, leaving a ten-metre crater. NATO scrambled fighters, activated a wide range of air defences and said it would "defend territory"; Poland blamed Russia. No Article 4 or Article 5 process was reported and there were no Polish casualties. |
| "Russia is achieving an operational breakthrough in Donbas" | Two independent estimates put the past month's gain at between zero and ten square miles. The Economist recorded **zero square miles** over the thirty days to July 28; DeepState OSINT data recorded a **net ten square miles** over the four weeks from June 30 to July 28, against thirty-one in the prior four-week period — against 226 recorded combat clashes on July 30 alone. |
| "Venezuela's transition talks will include the opposition's strongest figure" | They opened without her. María Corina Machado ruled out participating in the August 1 talks while stating she does not oppose them proceeding; the government side is led by Jorge Rodríguez, brother of interim president Delcy Rodríguez, and the opposition side by Dinorah Figuera. |
| "Falling crude will finally reach the pump" | The divergence closed the month in the same direction as it opened it. Brent rose 3.87% to $90.24 on July 31, closing July up roughly 24% — its strongest month since March — while diesel set another war high at $5.3530 and regular reached $4.1060. Diesel has now risen on every day of the past week irrespective of the direction of crude, and sits within about 46 cents of the all-time record. |
| "The Selective Service rule withdrawal has been reversed or explained" | Neither, nine days on. The automatic draft-registration rule withdrawn on July 23 has not been re-proposed and no explanation has been given. The December 19, 2026 statutory deadline stands, but no implementing rule is pending. Automatic registration is not a draft; none has been called or planned. |
| "Trump's threatened 'beating' would again be delivered outside Iran, as the July 28 Iraq strikes were" | It was not. Overnight July 29-30 CENTCOM completed a "heavy wave" against "dozens" of IRGC targets on Iranian territory — the first US munitions on Iranian soil since July 24 and, per a US official, about twice the size of the previous bombardment. The six-day interval in which the US struck Iran's proxies but not Iran is over. |
| "The strike pause of July 24-26 marked the end of the shooting phase of the war" | Definitively no. The pause broke from the Iranian side on July 28 with an intercepted ballistic salvo, the US answered in Iraq on July 28, Iran claimed the Jordan strike and struck three tankers on July 29, and the US struck Iranian territory at roughly double scale on July 29-30. The reciprocal halt lasted four days. The prior CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED reading of the pause ("operational reset for something bigger" vs "genuine de-escalation") is now RESOLVED against both framings: it ended in a unilateral US wave triggered by Iranian escalation, not in a joint US-Israeli campaign and not in de-escalation. |
| "A US ground operation follows once the air campaign resumes at scale" | Still no, on Day 155. The air campaign resumed at roughly double its previous scale and the ground rung did not move: no landing, no Kharg strike in the wave, no new ARG, MEU or ground-formation order, ~50,000 personnel unchanged, and no ground option named by the President, the Pentagon or CENTCOM. The one genuinely ambiguous datum — that the target set was coastal surveillance, coastal defence and maritime capability along the littoral — is equally consistent with the interdiction campaign a blockading navy runs, and is recorded as CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED rather than as evidence of intent. |
| "The war is geographically confined to Iran, the Gulf and its immediate approaches" | Not since July 29. An unclaimed drone struck the US-owned FSRU *Energos Winter* and the LNG carrier *Gaslog Salem* at Egypt's Damietta on the Mediterranean — the first attack on Egyptian soil of the war, roughly 2,000 km from the Strait of Hormuz, and the first anywhere in this conflict against an energy IMPORT terminal rather than an export chokepoint or production facility. Attribution is unresolved: Trump blamed Iran without evidence; Egypt confirmed a drone and named no one. |
| "Saudi Arabia has now committed to the war alongside the United States" | Both, and in consecutive days. Saudi jets flew joint precision strikes with CENTCOM in Iraq on July 28 — Riyadh's first claimed strikes inside Iraq of the war — and on July 29 the Saudi defence minister carried a message to the Oval Office that the Crown Prince favours diplomacy over a wider regional war and that Netanyahu is the party pushing escalation. Riyadh is defending itself kinetically while lobbying against escalation. |
| "Iran's promised same-day retaliation for the July 30 wave materialised" | Not by the cycle close. The IRGC said "with the help of God Almighty, the aggressor will be punished today" and warned states aiding the US of a "harsh response," but no further Iranian strike had been confirmed when the cycle closed. Iran's claims of prior damage — three F-35s destroyed at Al Azraq and US personnel killed — were denied by CENTCOM as to aircraft and left unaddressed as to personnel. |
| "Falling crude will finally reach the pump" | Still no, in the opposite direction this time. Brent surged 7.9% on July 29 and eased back below $90 on July 30, while the AAA national average rose on both grades — regular to $4.0980 and diesel to $5.3390, another war high. Diesel has risen on every day of the past week regardless of which way crude moved. Distillate tightness, not crude, is setting the diesel print. |
| "The Strait of Hormuz reopened overnight on July 30" | No such thing is established. The straits.live tracker printed 35 tankers transiting and 9 dark tankers against 10-13 and 68 a day earlier — while simultaneously printing 1,357 stranded vessels against 339, a move that does not reconcile with the other two as a single physical event. No methodology note was published and no independent source corroborated any of the three. IMF PortWatch's most recent independent count remains 10 commercial transits on July 23 against an 88-per-day pre-crisis baseline. The IRGC asserted on July 30 that it retains "full control" of the Strait. |
| "A Russian missile landing on NATO soil triggers an Article 5 cascade" | It did not, again. NATO confirmed a Russian missile entered Polish airspace on July 30 and scrambled jets; Warsaw's response was an emergency meeting, an investigation and an explicit refusal to attribute before certainty — Tusk saying "we want to be 100% certain about the type of missile and who launched it" and noting no direct threat because it landed in an uninhabited area. |
| "Cuba's fuel and power crisis is producing regime collapse" | The response has been economic liberalisation, not collapse. Following the fourth island-wide grid failure of 2026 on July 27, Havana announced its largest private-sector opening of the crisis — easing restrictions on private business and approving private imports of goods and medicines. |
| "Iran's reciprocal halt means Tehran is finished attacking US forces and shipping" | It resumed on both. On July 29 the IRGC claimed the ballistic strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base and a CENTCOM centre in Jordan — five missiles intercepted — and separately said it had struck and stopped three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, its first claimed shipping strikes since the halt, declaring that "the resistance will continue" as long as US actions do. |
| "Trump's promised retaliation means US strikes on Iranian territory resumed" | They did not. Trump said Iran was "going to get a beating" and "we'll be hitting them hard," but the actual US kinetic response was a joint CENTCOM-Saudi air strike on militia logistics hubs and weapons storage sites in IRAQ. The United States has not struck Iranian territory since July 24 — six days as of the cycle close. |
| "A US ground operation follows once the air campaign stalls" | Still no, and two of its preconditions moved backward in the same cycle. The air campaign against Iranian territory has been halted since July 24 while the war escalated on the ballistic, maritime and proxy-air rungs. Meanwhile the Selective Service withdrew its automatic draft-registration rule on July 23 after four months of White House inaction, and Britain and France refused to lead the only force generation actually under way — an allied naval escort coalition. |
| "Oman's Gulf-backed plan gives the Strait of Hormuz a negotiated transit regime" | Iran rejected it on July 29 and counterproposed the opposite. Against Oman's 50-50 lane split funded by voluntary Malacca-model contributions, Tehran demanded one route entirely within Iranian territorial waters plus part of the other, oversight of both inbound and outbound traffic, and a reported $1 million per ship "service fee." Gharibabadi: "If the Strait of Hormuz returns to its previous state, our success in this war is not complete." |
| "The London conference will produce a multinational Hormuz escort coalition" | Not yet, and not with the leaders Washington wanted. POLITICO reported that Hegseth is urging the UK and France to help lead the mission and that European allies are refusing "until they see an enduring ceasefire in the Iran war," with sources expecting no movement soon. Iran separately declared any third-party mine-clearing vessel near the Strait a "legitimate target," attacking the mission's core premise. |
| "Saudi Arabia will stay out of the shooting war" | It did not. On July 28 the Saudi Arabian Armed Forces flew joint precision strikes with CENTCOM against militia targets in Iraq — Riyadh's first claimed strikes inside Iraq since the war began — invoking Article 51 of the UN Charter and citing drones aimed at petroleum facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh region. |
| "China is staying out of the material side of the Iran war" | Contested, not settled. Reuters reported on three sources that Iran will receive within weeks the first of up to 400 Chinese QW-12/FN-16 MANPADS worth $60-70 million, routed from Urumqi through Pakistan via a Hong Kong intermediary. Beijing called the report "completely groundless" and Pakistan's military called it "absolutely concocted and false." Recorded as contested_unresolved, not as confirmed: see open-questions china-manpads-transfer-iran-july-2026. |
| "Falling crude will finally reach the pump" | Still no — and the divergence now runs both ways. Diesel rose on every day of a three-session, roughly $14 Brent decline to a fresh war high of $5.329, while regular slipped to $4.091 on the very day Brent rebounded 3.43% back above $90. Distillate tightness, not crude, is setting the diesel print. |
| "The Pentagon's casualty reclassification was a temporary data anomaly that would be resolved imminently" | Two days on it has not been reversed, and the department has now supplied a substantive rationale instead: a Pentagon official said that "because Operation Epic Fury has concluded" the latest casualties are classified separately — while declining to give any date on which the operation ended. Total wounded across both categories now stands at 642. |
| "An automatic draft registration rule is on track for December 2026" | The rule was withdrawn on July 23, 2026 after the White House held it for nearly four months without acting. The December 19, 2026 statutory deadline is unchanged, but no implementing rule is now pending and neither the agency nor the White House has explained the withdrawal or announced a re-proposal. |
| "The two-sided strike pause marks the end of the shooting phase of the war" | It lasted four days. Iran's IRGC fired multiple ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East at 5:45 p.m. ET on July 28 in what CENTCOM called an "attempted surprise attack." All were intercepted and no casualties resulted, but the reciprocal halt Iran declared on July 26 did not hold. CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED as to whether the launch terminates Iran's halt or is a bounded signal: see `iran-strike-pause-reload-or-climbdown-july-2026`. |
| "Iran's missile campaign is spent — it can no longer reach US forces" | It reached them on July 28, and The Intercept reported the same day that Iran has fired 8,000-9,000 drones and missiles since February and struck at least nine US outposts since July 9, several with "significant" damage. What is depleting is the American interceptor inventory: more than 11,000 munitions expended in the first 16 days, with Patriot and THAAD stocks estimated three or more years from recovery. |
| "The Trump-Netanyahu meeting will produce a joint escalation decision against Iran's nuclear programme" | It did not. Trump publicly rebuffed the Israeli briefing on Pickaxe Mountain before the meeting ("I don't need Bibi to tell me that… he wants me to stay involved"), the session produced no announced operational decision, and Israel's own public-diplomacy chief said afterwards that Pickaxe did not come up. Trump's own framing kept the target conditional on diplomacy failing — "if we don't make a deal, we don't make a deal." CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — see `netanyahu-pickaxe-intelligence-escalation-july-2026`. |
| "A US ground operation follows once the air campaign stalls" | The air campaign stalled on July 24 and the ground rung did not move for five days. When the pause broke on July 28 it broke on the ballistic rung and from the Iranian side. Every US escalation option stated on the record that day was an air strike on a nuclear site, and the amphibious capability required for the reported Kharg options fell further: The War Zone's July 28 count confirms USS Boxer as the sole deployed ARG fleet-wide, with USS Tripoli home at Sasebo and no relief ARG announced. |
| "Falling crude will finally reach the pump" | Still no. Brent has fallen roughly $14 from the July 23 settle of $100.69 to about $86.58 on July 28, while the AAA national average for diesel rose on every day of that fall to a fresh war high of $5.321; regular eased by a tenth of a cent to $4.099. Retail has lagged every crude move of this war in both directions. |
| "An air-only ceasefire in Ukraine is under negotiation" | Only on one side of the record. Zelensky brought the proposal to the Oval Office on July 28 and Ukrainian and US officials had been working on it, but Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied that talks over an aerial ceasefire are under way at all, and Moscow warned intensified Ukrainian strikes inside Russia would prolong the war. |
| "The strike pause is a 48-hour operational reset before an immediate larger campaign" | It has now run three days and lengthened rather than closed. The Pentagon reportedly presented Trump a plan for a 14th consecutive night of strikes on July 26-27 and he declined to authorise it. Iran reciprocated and has held. The prediction is not yet falsified as to eventual resumption — Trump has promised strikes will return at "greater force" if talks fail — but the specific 24-48-hour reset framing (former Defense Secretary Mark Esper, July 25) has been overtaken. CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED as to intent: see `iran-strike-pause-reload-or-climbdown-july-2026`. |
| "The Pentagon's reported ground-operation options mean the US is moving toward a ground war in Iran" | *Foreign Policy*'s July 24 survey of former US military officials found the opposite: the United States "does not appear to be moving toward a major ground operation in Iran," which would require far more troops than the ~50,000 currently in the region. Retired Gen. Joseph Votel put the realistic case narrowly — "What we might see is the use of ground forces in limited raids." Meanwhile the 31st MEU named in that planning went home to Okinawa on July 22 with no relief ARG announced, and the only force generation actually under way is a multinational NAVAL coalition being assembled in London. |
| "Falling crude prices will quickly show up at the pump" | They have not. Brent fell two straight sessions from the July 23 settle of $100.69 into the $85-90 range by July 27, a decline of roughly $10-15, while the AAA national average held flat at $4.110 for regular and rose to $5.296 for diesel — both wartime highs. Retail has lagged every crude move of this war in both directions. |
| "The July air campaign will escalate monotonically until Iran capitulates" (widely forecast after Trump's July 23-25 'massive attack' and 'locked and loaded' statements) | The campaign STOPPED. Thirteen consecutive nights ended with no strikes into July 25 or July 26, Iran reciprocated its own halt on July 26, and the reported rationale was that the target set was "mostly exhausted" (Gen. Brad Cooper, via *Axios*) and air-defence interceptor stocks were thinning (Gen. Dan Caine). No "massive attack" was ordered. (Al Jazeera; CNN; Middle East Monitor citing *Axios*, July 25-26, 2026.) |
| "The Pentagon's reported ground-operation options mean a Kharg Island raid or seizure is imminent" | The assault force named in that planning left. The 31st MEU — identified in the March 2026 reporting, alongside the 82nd Airborne, as a unit that "could conduct raids and seizures" with Kharg among candidate targets — completed its deployment and offloaded ~2,500 Marines at Okinawa on July 22, 2026, with no relief amphibious ready group announced. The options remain reported-but-undecided; the capability to execute them fell. (*Stars and Stripes*; USNI News; Marine Corps Times, July 22, 2026.) |
| "America will never shut out Chinese students" | Trump admin aggressively revoking visas (May 2025) |
| "US-China rapprochement" | SCOTUS struck down IEEPA tariffs Feb 20; Trump imposed 10% global tariff under Section 122; China tariffs at 47%; truce extended but tensions remain; Trump-Xi summit May 14-15 |
| "Germany-Russia rapprochement" | Relations frozen; economic decoupling; policy explicitly rejects rapprochement |
| "Russia as nuclear guarantor preventing strikes on Iran" | Russia did NOT prevent strikes; treaty lacks mutual defense clause |
| "Coalition includes Saudi Arabia" | Saudi refused airspace, condemned strikes on Iran |
| Trump picks Nikki Haley as VP | Trump chose JD Vance |

### Hormuz Blockade & Regional Fallout
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 5):** **The ladder did not climb, and the world's largest tanker operator stopped waiting.** CENTCOM's tally held at **87 vessels redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded** for *“total compliance”* — unchanged from September 3, with **boarding still the highest rung of American physical intrusion in 191 days** against zero landings, zero raids and zero seizures of territory. **Six transits** against an **85/day** pre-crisis baseline (**7% of normal**); weekly transits **102** against **130+/day** pre-war; the Strait recorded as **closed to commercial shipping**; war-risk insurance at **40.0× pre-crisis**, hull rates **7.5-10% of vessel value** per transit, claims **~$2bn** across 70+ cases, and **$7-8 of every barrel** attributable to war-risk insurance per *Lloyd's List*. **Mitsui O.S.K. Lines** withdrew its resumption timeline entirely — *“it's difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year”* — abandoning a prior assumption of phased October resumption and normal January operations, with **no plan to return without guarantees of sustainably safe passage**. **Iraq is routing around the problem from both ends:** Baghdad has begun a cabinet-approved process to hire tankers for Hormuz runs through the state-run **Iraqi Oil Tankers Co.** because commercial owners will not take the risk, while **SOMO** allocates **3.017m bpd** of Basra crude for September and continues offering **Basrah Medium and Heavy for ship-to-ship collection near the Omani coast**, outside the Strait. **Saudi Arabia** still moves **1.9m bpd** through the **Egyptian pipeline** to the Mediterranean, into a Red Sea whose war-risk area was extended **800km** up the kingdom's west coast. **Bangladesh's LNG imports fell ~83% in a month** (0.63m → 0.11m tonnes) against a projected **$2.8bn** increase in its 2026 fuel bill; the **EU** has absorbed **~€41bn** in extra fossil-fuel costs since March with gas at **~€74.5/MWh**, the highest intraday level since **January 2023**, and winter inventories abnormally low; **US retail gasoline $4.14/gal**. **De Nederlandsche Bank moved ~86 tonnes of gold (~$10-12bn) out of New York and Ottawa to London between March and August, citing “increasing geopolitical unrest.”** Reopening probabilities: **September 15 <1%; September 30 2%; December 31 27% (from 28%); January 1, 2027 22%.**
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 4):** **The blockade climbed to boarding, the risk zone spread to the bypass, and the cost of the war was priced per barrel for the first time.** CENTCOM's tally reached **87 vessels redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded** for **“total compliance”** as of **September 3**, from **83 redirected / 3 disabled** on September 2 and **67 / 3 / 2** on August 20. **The Institute for the Study of War** assessed Iran's ability to **surveil the Strait and lay mines** as likely **significantly degraded**, citing the IRGC's fallback to **shore-based rocket launchers** for mining and **fast-attack craft to physically identify vessels** because only a few radars still cover the southern route; ISW counted **~40 vessels** transiting on September 1. **Iran's counter-instrument is regulatory:** the **Persian Gulf Strait Authority** blacklisted **11 more vessels**, taking the list to **56** from 45 a week earlier, with **fines, detention or confiscation** threatened and cooperation with a listed hull itself listable; **at least three Indian refiners and one global energy major** will stop using listed ships. **Oman refused Iran's joint transit-fee scheme outright**, including the voluntary version, per a senior regional official — foreclosing the only littoral cover for a toll regime. **The insurance ledger was published:** ~**$2bn in war-risk claims** across **70+ cases** and **72+ ship attacks since March**, the **second-largest marine underwriting loss in over a decade**; premiums **40-60× pre-crisis**; hull rates up to **10% of ship value** per transit; **$10.0m per VLCC transit** on the straits.live board; and **$7-8 of every barrel of crude down to war-risk insurance alone** (David Osler, *Lloyd's List*). **The risk area extended 800 km up Saudi Arabia's west coast** with the **Houthis targeting Yanbu**, placing the **1.9m bpd Egyptian-pipeline bypass** inside a war-risk zone of its own. **Transit counts remain irreconcilable:** the board carries **6 transits vs an 85/day baseline (7%)**, **134 vessels transiting**, **402 holding position** and **51 of 244 screened tankers AIS-dark in 24 hours**, against administration claims of **15-18m barrels a night**. **The Philippine ledger:** since February 28, **31 vessels carrying 421 Filipino seafarers attacked — 406 unharmed, 10 injured, 3 killed, 1 missing.** **South Korea is preparing a Hormuz naval deployment before year-end** — the **Cheonghae Unit's** destroyer ***Wang Geon***, ~**260 personnel** with a **boarding team** and Lynx helicopters, requiring **National Assembly approval**.
- **CURRENT STATUS (August 22):** The **US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains ACTIVE and has hardened.** CENTCOM's tally reached **67 commercial vessels redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded** as of August 20, from **35 redirected / 2 disabled / 2 boarded** on August 2 and **44 redirected** on August 3. On **August 11** a US Navy helicopter fired **two Hellfire missiles into the engine room of the Panama-flagged container ship *Vela Nova*** in the Gulf of Oman, disabling its steering gear after the crew ignored repeated warnings while attempting to reach an Iranian port. **TRAFFIC:** PortWatch logged **one transit on August 9** against a **73-per-day pre-crisis baseline**; **thirteen vessels** transited on August 16 (four inbound, nine outbound); five crossed on August 15 and **none on August 16** against thirty-one the previous weekend; the prior week ran at about **4% of pre-war levels**. straits.live counted **314 hulls holding position away from berth on August 18 and 386 on August 21**, with 542 Hormuz-area port arrivals in 24 hours and the Hormuz Index composite in its **extreme** band. **War-risk cover for a transit is running near 10% of hull value**, with insurers trimming quotas and some withdrawing. Estimation is degrading as more vessels transit with trackers off and ship-to-ship transfers disguise volumes. **GOVERNANCE IS CONTESTED BY ANNOUNCEMENT:** Iran's **August 6-7 Oman-brokered arrangement** bars **American and Israeli vessels outright**, fines violators **up to 20% of cargo value**, denies passage to states and individuals deemed to have damaged Iran until compensation is paid, and assigns Iran navigation guidance, vessel-traffic monitoring, maritime security and environmental protection, with Iranian officials overseeing inbound and Omani officials outbound traffic; **Washington rejected it** and any "impediments." Iran's parliament speaker states the strait **"will not reopen until US sanctions are lifted and frozen assets released"**; Trump says **"we have total control over the strait,"** calls the blockade a **"wall of steel"** and likes **"the idea of declaring it a territory"** — see open question `hormuz-control-attribution-august-2026`. **REGIONAL FALLOUT:** the World Bank has cut its 2026 GCC growth forecast from **4.4% to 1.3%**, with **Kuwait and Qatar expected to contract**; roughly **80 energy facilities** struck for an estimated **$58 billion**; Qatar has lost about **17% of LNG export capacity** to the March Ras Laffan strike. Downstream, Qatar and the UAE supply **99% of Pakistan's LNG, 72% of Bangladesh's and 53% of India's**; South Korea runs **licence-plate vehicle rationing**, Japan and South Korea are drawing on their **joint stockpile**, **Indonesia caps fuel at 50 litres a day and Sri Lanka at 15**, Pakistan has suspended **~78 mmcfd** of LNG to its fertiliser sector, and Bangladesh expects to lose **40 of 115 scheduled 2026 cargoes** with **four of five state urea plants shut** and power-sector gas cut from **870 to 820 mmcfd**. Maritime premiums across the region are up **300-400%**. **PIRACY HAS FILLED THE VACUUM:** Somali pirates hijacked the sanctioned Iranian shadow-fleet tanker **SIBU 1** on August 20, the second hijacking in four days, with **13 incidents in the first seven months of 2026 against five in all of 2025** — the highest in a decade. (CENTCOM; Al Jazeera; straits.live; PortWatch; Lloyd's List Intelligence; Business Insurance; AGBI; Wood Mackenzie; IEEFA; LightCastle Partners; gCaptain; CNBC, August 2-21, 2026.)
- **CURRENT STATUS (August 1):** The **US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains ACTIVE**; the CENTCOM interdiction tally is unchanged at **18 vessels stopped, 2 disabled, 2 boarded** with 20+ warships committed. **Traffic ticked up but throughput did not recover:** S&P Global recorded **28 Hormuz transits on July 29**, the highest since July 14, driven by **resumed LNG tanker traffic after a two-week gap**, with Iran-linked vessels at **60% of movements** (from a 68% second-half-of-July average); **Bab el-Mandeb crossings rose to 39** and VLCCs increasingly gathered at **Egypt's Sidi Kerir**. The straits.live board **reverted to its prior framing** — latest recorded volume **10 transits** against an **88/day pre-crisis baseline (11% of normal)**, **1,364 stranded**, **85 AIS-dark tankers** against a 42.4 seven-day baseline, war-risk insurance at **8.0x peacetime** — confirming the July 30 print as a measurement change rather than a reopening. Iran's Fars agency said the IRGC **stopped two tankers** and **four others altered course**. **Iran's rejection of Oman's 50-50 lane split stands**, as does its counterproposal for the inbound lane entirely under Iranian control. **Riyadh convened 43 nations on July 30** for a maritime defence coalition covering the Bab al-Mandeb, Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, headquartered in the kingdom, with thirteen public backers — while **Britain and France still refuse to co-lead the US Hormuz escort coalition**. **Yanbu** handled roughly **92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June 2026** and sits inside the Houthi blockade zone declared July 20. - **CURRENT STATUS (July 26):** The **US naval blockade of Iranian ports is ACTIVE and "in full effect"** — re-imposed July 14 after a ~27-day lift, and explicitly maintained through the July 25-26 strike pause. Cumulative enforcement since re-imposition: **12 commercial vessels redirected, 2 disabled, 2 boarded**; Iran's IRGC has separately **stopped six vessels with warning shots**, and one tanker was reported to have **struck a mine**. Governance of the Strait is the live negotiation: **Iranian and Omani deputy foreign ministers met in Tehran July 24-25** and reported progress on "shared principles and operational mechanisms for managing the safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while respecting the sovereign rights of the two coastal states" — an Iran-Oman **co-management** formula Washington and the Gulf states have rejected — while Iran's foreign ministry says the Strait's status **"remains unchanged"** pending a deal and objects to the US-backed alternative route near Oman. **Traffic is at the lowest level of the war:** Windward recorded **one vessel (a Comoros-flagged general cargo ship, outbound) and zero tankers in either direction** in the 24 hours to July 25, with a 12-hour window of no crossings — under 2% of the 88/day pre-crisis baseline, below the 15 transits IMF PortWatch logged July 19; roughly 85 tankers run dark and the IMO still assesses the waterway as too dangerous for commercial transit. **Second chokepoint contested:** the Houthi maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia declared July 20 stands, and the July 25 strikes on Aramco at **Jizan** (refinery ablaze) and **Yanbu** hit the outlet of the East-West Pipeline, which handled ~92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June 2026 — leaving the Kingdom interdicted on both flanks with no third corridor. **Brent ~$91/bbl** after a >5% fall on the strike pause; **AAA pump averages $4.111 regular / $5.295 diesel**. (Al Jazeera; Fortune/AP; CBS News; Windward; IMF PortWatch; TechTimes; TradingEconomics; AAA, July 20-26, 2026.)

### Venezuela, Cuba, Colombia
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 5):** **The economic premise of the intervention was priced, and it is measured in decades.** *The National* reports the **~$100bn** American bet on Venezuelan crude facing a years-long wait: extra-heavy reserves requiring upgraders that **“you just cannot build in a couple of years”** (Kpler), **~1.4m bpd by 2028**, **at most 300,000 bpd of additions by 2030**, **3m bpd only by 2040**, greenfield output **not before 2033-34**, against **Energy Secretary Chris Wright's** projection of **2m bpd by decade's end**. Analysts question whether acting president **Delcy Rodríguez** can lawfully grant **100-year rights** over 17 fields holding **65 billion barrels**; **Trump says a century, Rodríguez says twenty-five years**. **Chevron** has committed **>$7bn over five years** to ~600,000 bpd, with **Eni** and **GE Vernova** alongside; US-bound exports are up **238% to ~515,000 bpd**. **The Maduro prosecution now has a full calendar: prosecution response due October 2, Hellerstein hearing November 17, trial June 1, 2027**, with Maduro in a **Brooklyn federal jail** arguing status-based head-of-state immunity through counsel **Barry Pollack**, and **Cilia Flores** claiming spousal protection. The **State Department sanctioned five Cuban companies and a grandson of Raúl Castro** over **nickel mining and energy**, on an island whose fuel reserves are **exhausted**, where some areas take **20-22 hours of blackout daily**, which suffered its **sixth nationwide grid failure of 2026** in August, and where **one Russian tanker** has docked since January. **SOUTHCOM** intercepted and sank another vessel, allegedly refuelling **Los Choneros** trafficking operations. At the theatre's edges: **Haiti's** foreign minister asked the Security Council to renew the international force mandate before **December elections** as a third consecutive Thursday deportation flight landed, and **Milei** escalated sanctions against companies in a **Falklands** offshore oil project.
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 4):** **The Venezuela file entered its first real legal test, and the argument reaches back to the capture.** **Nicolás Maduro** and **Cilia Flores** filed **separate motions** in Manhattan federal court on **September 2** seeking dismissal of the narco-terrorism indictment; counsel **Barry Pollack** argued the court **lacks jurisdiction** because sovereign heads of state enjoy **complete immunity** and because the acts alleged **would have been official duties**, and that Maduro **remained Venezuela's head of state notwithstanding US non-recognition**. Flores claims **spousal** protection. Judge **Alvin Hellerstein** hears the motions on **November 17**; trial remains **June 1, 2027**. **If immunity attached at the time of the acts and of the seizure, the January 2026 US military operation that removed both from Venezuela was the abduction of a serving head of state — which puts the legality of the operation, not only the sufficiency of the charges, before a US district judge for the first time.** **Delcy Rodríguez's** government is unaffected and the **August 28 hundred-year concession** over fields holding **65 billion barrels**, to a joint venture in which the **US government holds 55%**, stands. **Cuba:** the energy and mines ministry says **all fuel reserves are exhausted**, with **20-22 hour daily blackouts** in some areas, an **eighth nationwide outage since late 2024** and the **third of 2026**; since January the United States has permitted **one oil tanker — Russian — to dock**. **Colombia:** a **UN fact-finding mission** on Sudan reported **up to 2,000 Colombian contractors** operating drone systems for the **Rapid Support Forces** inside a supply network naming the **UAE, Chad, Libya and Somalia**; the UAE rejected the allegations and **Bogotá said it opposes mercenarism**.
- **CURRENT STATUS (August 22):** **The Venezuelan talks opened and held; Colombia swung right; Cuba's grid failed again.** US-backed government-opposition negotiations began in **Caracas on August 6** after days of delay, with **Jorge Rodríguez** — National Assembly president and brother of acting president **Delcy Rodríguez** — leading for the government and **Dinorah Figuera** for the 2015 National Assembly bloc, on an agenda of democratic institutions, electoral reform and political participation; Figuera seeks a trustworthy CNE and a Supreme Court reconstituted throughout its structure. **María Corina Machado was not invited**; she says she will not obstruct "real progress" but will judge by restored institutions, freed political prisoners and scheduled elections, and she and **Edmundo González Urrutia** state their camp had **no involvement whatsoever** — the opposition counterparty is contested. This is Venezuela's **ninth dialogue in twelve years**. **COLOMBIA:** **Abelardo de la Espriella** was inaugurated the country's 36th president on **August 7 in Cali**, the first inauguration outside Bogotá, rejecting Petro's negotiations, ceasefires and concessions, committing to **"Plan Patriota 2.0"** with Washington (announced after a July 21 meeting between his incoming defence minister and US Assistant Secretary of Defense **Joseph M. Humire**), and proposing to cut ties with **Venezuela, Nicaragua and Cuba** while aligning with the US and Israel; on **August 10** Colombian forces killed two alleged **ELN** members in a raid near the Venezuelan border. **CUBA:** the national grid collapsed late on **August 2**, the island's **sixth nationwide blackout of 2026**, with thunderstorms disrupting restoration on August 3 after three failures in nine days in July; fuel remains the proximate cause, with Venezuelan supply reduced and Mexican imports ceased. On **August 20** the US Treasury and State Department sanctioned **nine Cuban state-owned companies and the leadership of the Cuban Institute**, targeting mining and construction. **MADURO:** Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores remain in US custody awaiting trial before **Judge Alvin Hellerstein on June 1, 2027**. ### Russia-Ukraine War (April 2026)
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 5):** **For the first time in this reference's tracking of the theatre, the ceasefire prediction has a dated test window.** **Witkoff** and **Kushner** go to **Moscow on September 5** and **Kyiv on September 6** with what **Trump** calls **“a proposal to end the war”** — their first Kyiv visit and first Moscow trip since **January 2026**; **Peskov** declined to confirm the Moscow leg. **Zelensky** publicly pledged **“we will not carry out any airstrikes”** and to **“ensure the normal functioning of Russian airspace”** for the duration, asking Russia to reciprocate; ***Ukrainska Pravda*** reports an **unannounced order for Ukrainian units to hold fire along the front from September 5 to 8**, sourced to multiple brigades and a senior security official, with **no official acknowledgement** and no published scope. **Putin** said an agreement is possible and that several countries **including the United States and China** are ready to support a settlement; **Moscow has not responded to the offer.** Hours before it was made, a **Russian drone struck the SBU headquarters in central Kyiv in daylight, wounding twelve** — Zelensky said it targeted the SBU chief's office, and Foreign Minister **Sybiha** called the timing Moscow's **“true rejection of diplomacy.”** Cycle dead: **Odesa** 1, **Dnipro** 2 police officers, **Belgorod** 4 including medical personnel from a Ukrainian strike, **Donetsk** 3 civilians; Ukrainian drones burned oil depots near **Sochi** and **Sirius**. **The front is described as largely deadlocked.** Two alliance strains, both financial: **Slovakia is the sole holdout** on the EU's twelve-month sanctions rollover, and **Trump has indicated he wants European reimbursement for American aid already delivered**. The hybrid campaign widened again — a **Geoscan 701** drone on a Finnish shoreline east of Helsinki, attempted **electricity-grid sabotage in Germany**, an **arson investigation at a Munich defence firm**.
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 4):** **The war's centre of gravity moved west of the front again — a German airport, a Polish factory, a Danish recruitment network and a Belgian veto.** **Ursula von der Leyen** called Russian drone incidents over Europe the **“new normal,”** cited Moscow's growing **“recklessness”** and promised **additional sanctions** after Berlin blamed Russia for an **explosive-laden drone with a detonator found at Leipzig/Halle Airport** — a civilian freight hub, **NATO logistics node** and base for Ukraine's **Antonov An-124** fleet — and **ordered a Russian consulate closed**; Moscow retaliated by shutting **Goethe-Institut** centres. EU foreign ministers are to announce a **“clear response”** within the week. **Donald Tusk** blamed Russia for **“deliberate arson”** at the **WB Electronics** drone factory supplying Ukraine; Denmark's **PET** reported Russia **recruiting Danish citizens through social media and gaming platforms** for sabotage planning against Ukrainian defence suppliers. **Belgium's Maxime Prevot** said opposition to spending **frozen Russian assets** is unchanged and the latest attempt to reopen it met **“little enthusiasm”** — the Euroclear veto holds. Ukraine's **Mykola Kalashynk** asked **ICAO** to ban all operations in Russian airspace. **On the line:** the General Staff's 08:00 report for **September 3** recorded **215 clashes** in 24 hours, **Pokrovsk (31 attacks)** and **Kostiantynivka (25)** the hottest sectors, against **98 Russian airstrikes and 353 guided aerial bombs**. **Odesa** took **17 wounded** and a damaged **21-storey block**; **Kyiv** took a **seventh consecutive night** of drone attack after 11 wounded the night before. Kyiv's cumulative Russian-loss claim is **~1,492,350** since February 2022 (+1,320 in 24h) — a Ukrainian figure, not independently verified. **Erdoğan** offered Turkish mediation; **no negotiation is scheduled and no Article 4 consultation was requested over Leipzig.**
- **CURRENT STATUS (August 22):** **Moscow is now building its campaign around the interceptor gap the Iran war created, and has accepted spillover into NATO states.** Ukraine's GUR deputy head **Maj. Gen. Vadym Skibitskyi** said on **August 10** that Russia has been **reprioritising ballistic and cruise missile production since April 2026 specifically to exploit Ukrainian Patriot shortages**, and has **more than tripled monthly ballistic launches between April and July**. The shortage is downstream of the Iran war: CSIS puts remaining US Patriot stocks under **827** against roughly **2,200** pre-war, with **60%+ of Patriot and THAAD expended** and **three-plus years to rebuild**, after Zelensky said on **August 1** that Ukraine had **run out of interceptors** — one of twenty-seven ballistic missiles downed in a barrage that killed nine to ten in Kyiv. On **August 8** Ukraine's Strategic Communications Centre reported, citing US intelligence, that Russia is preparing a **major strike campaign against Kyiv's energy infrastructure ahead of Independence Day on August 24**; Zelensky said the same day that Ukraine has **effectively no undamaged power plants left**. On **August 20** Russian drones penetrated **Moldovan and Romanian airspace** and Romania scrambled **two F-16s** to destroy an explosive naval drone near a **Black Sea gas platform**; **ISW assessed that the Kremlin has accepted the risk that its war will damage other states, including NATO members** — and **no Article 4 consultation followed**. ISW also assessed on August 20 that **war veterans will likely be seated in the State Duma at the September 2026 elections** as part of militarising Russian society, and that Moscow's response to domestic **gasoline shortages** remains inadequate; neither the Kremlin nor Russian milbloggers believe Russia can fully intercept Ukrainian strike packages soon. **Ukrainian forces advanced northeast of Kharkiv City**, and ISW's standing assessment that Russia's **spring-summer 2026 offensive failed to achieve operationally significant gains** is unrevised, as is its July 31 finding that Russia's **Northern Grouping is likely misreporting gains to the Kremlin**. **No negotiating round convened in this cycle.** (ISW, August 8, 10 and 20, 2026, via Kyiv Post and Critical Threats; RFE/RL; CNBC; WSJ and Reuters via Just Security, August 21, 2026; CSIS.)
- **CURRENT STATUS (August 1):** **A Russian cruise missile detonated on NATO territory.** A projectile assessed by experts as a **Kh-101** crossed into Polish airspace during Russia's overnight barrage and exploded in a field near **Tarnawa-Kolonia**, outside **Lublin**, leaving a **ten-metre crater**; **NATO scrambled fighters, activated a wide range of air defences and said it would "defend territory,"** and Warsaw blamed Moscow. No Polish casualties. **The barrage itself:** 70+ missiles and ~280 drones against **Kyiv and Lviv**, killing **at least eight including three children** (later counts nine, then ten). **Ukraine answered deep:** on July 31 long-range strikes hit **oil refineries and Wildberries logistics facilities in Volgograd, Tatarstan and Krasnodar**, after Zelensky's July 30 pledge to intensify strikes on Russian territory. **The line is nearly static:** 226 combat clashes by 22:00 July 30, heaviest at **Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk**; The Economist puts Russia's 30-day gain at **zero square miles** and DeepState the four-week net at **ten** (against 31 in the prior period). Ukrainian negotiator **Sergiy Kyslytsya** argues Kyiv now has leverage because the deep-strike campaign is causing Russian fuel shortages; **66% of Ukrainians** want a negotiated end as soon as possible. (The Washington Post; Al Jazeera; Foreign Policy; The Irish Times; Stars and Stripes; CNN; NPR; TIME; Mezha/Bukvy; Charter'97; ISW; Russia Matters, July 28-31, 2026.)

On the ground, Kostiantynivka has become Russia's main objective (Russian forces entered its northeastern part and achieved a tactical breakthrough in the west; advancing along the T-0504 toward the railway station). Formal peace talks remain frozen (Kremlin rejected new talks; Zelenskyy issued five conditions to the E3 in London). The Pokrovsk sector remained the heaviest along the front, with Russia still unable to advance significantly west of Pokrovsk/Myrnohrad (Kyiv Independent "Ukraine, Russia conclude talks in Istanbul"; RFE/RL "After Round Two Of Russia-Ukraine Talks, Peace Seems Even More Elusive"; Wikipedia "Pokrovsk offensive")

### US-China Trade
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 5):** **The Hormuz campaign became visible in Chinese refinery runs.** Preliminary **Kpler** figures put Chinese imports of Iranian crude at **~534,000 bpd in August** against **~823,000 bpd in July** and a **1.4m bpd** average last year; **September and October offers have collapsed**, and **Shandong teapots** are substituting **Russian Urals and fuel oil** because **ESPO sold out weeks ago**, with **throughput cuts expected in October**. **That reduction was achieved by naval blockade rather than by any American action against a Chinese entity, and it lands three weeks before the summit.** **Xi** is expected at the **White House on September 24** in a compressed visit — arriving late **September 23**, departing **September 25**, **skipping the UN General Assembly** — with a state dinner planned and expectations reported as low. The dated instrument behind the meeting is **November 10**, when China's **suspended rare-earth export controls including the extraterritorial measures can snap back** absent a new agreement, one week after the **November 3** midterms. In the Pacific, island leaders raised concerns over China's **July ICBM test** that overflew their nations **without adequate warning**, with **Nauru dissenting** from the collective statement and Beijing's foreign ministry reaffirming **“peaceful development.”** **No Taiwan incident, exercise, export-control action or tariff this cycle**; Nvidia **H200** approvals and the multi-year agricultural purchase commitments (**$17bn/yr**, **25m tonnes of soybeans/yr**, 2026-2028) stand unchanged.
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 4):** **Xi spent the week offering the Middle East a security order without an outside enforcer, and he did it at the alternative chokepoint.** Concluding the **first Chinese state visit to Egypt in a decade** (September 1-3, following the **Bishkek SCO summit**), Xi called on Middle Eastern countries to **oppose external interference**, urged them to consider **reshaping the region's security order**, and offered **Chinese cooperation on protecting shipping routes** — said beside the **Suez Canal**, which the Hormuz blockade has made the principal alternative energy corridor and through whose pipeline **Saudi Arabia is now moving 1.9m bpd** to the Mediterranean. Trump is due to host Xi at the **White House on September 24**, with a **state dinner** planned and **Beijing yet to confirm**; expectations are being managed down on both sides, with Iran sanctions and unresolved technology disputes — AI, cyber, export controls, digital sovereignty — the principal frictions. The **May Beijing summit** produced Chinese purchases of at least **$17bn of US agricultural goods annually through 2028** and a new **US-China Board of Trade and Board of Investment**; the average US tariff on Chinese goods stood at **36.5% as of July**. **Enforcement ran the other way:** the United States is investigating Singapore-based **Apex Logistics** for facilitating illegal semiconductor shipments to China — potentially the **first legal action against a transportation company for chip smuggling**, extending export-control liability to the logistics layer — and imposed **tariffs of up to 100% on drones over 55 pounds or using thermal imaging**, almost all Chinese-made and widely used in the US for **wildfire tracking and search-and-rescue**. Beijing is pressing for answers on the death of Chinese national **Lianyong Wei** in **ICE custody**. **Taiwan:** no military incident; Taiwanese exports to the US up **33.7%** after the tariff cut to **15%** on many goods.
- **CURRENT STATUS (August 22):** **The sanctions phase collides with Beijing, and the commercial facts move without Beijing's consent.** China **rejected US pressure on August 20-21**, restating that sanctions will not resolve disputes, as Trump threatened penalties on any country extending Tehran **"any type of lifeline"** and Bessent promised **"the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world."** Yet **Chinese imports of Iranian crude fell to 534,000 bpd in August from 823,000 in July**, with fewer September and October cargo offers, prices up, Chinese independent **"teapot" refiners on alert for buyer-specific designations**, and roughly **40 million barrels stranded in Malaysian waters**. Beijing's substantive position is unchanged — settle through negotiation, carry out the MOU, avoid resorting to force, **support for Iran diplomatic only**; the Reuters MANPADS report remains **denied by both Beijing and Islamabad and unverified**. **TAIWAN:** Taipei ran its annual **Han Kuang exercise from August 5-14** — its largest drills of the year, with air-raid exercises and a deliberate temporary **mobile-internet slowdown** — and on **August 21** Taiwan's coast guard warned off a **Chinese research ship** in western waters, the **third appearance since May**; no new PLA blockade-style exercise was announced. **HONG KONG:** **Lee Cheuk-yan** and **Chow Hang-tung** were convicted on **August 21** under the national security law of inciting subversion over the Tiananmen vigils. **CALENDAR UNMOVED:** Xi's **White House visit expected around September 24**; tariff exclusions on **178 Chinese products to November 10, 2026**; the USTR's **12.5% Section 301 forced-labour tariff** (effective July 24) the operative new measure; **$17bn/yr** of US agricultural purchases through 2028 and the rare-earth export-restriction halt from the May summit stand, against Xi's unresolved warning that mishandling Taiwan would put the relationship in **"great jeopardy."** **BALANCE OF CAPABILITY:** more than **60% of US Patriot and THAAD stocks expended** with three-plus years to rebuild, and roughly **one-third of the Tomahawk inventory depleted** after 1,000-plus fired, answered by a **$22.9bn seven-year Raytheon contract** — a constraint on any Taiwan contingency produced entirely by another theatre. Roughly **40% of Chinese oil imports transit Hormuz**, where traffic runs at 1-13 vessels a day against 73. (Reuters and AP via Just Security, August 21, 2026; CNBC; Asharq Al-Awsat; CSIS; Defense News.)
- **JULY 24 UPDATE**: The US imposed a **fresh tariff wave on ~60 countries** (incl. China, Japan, South Korea, India, EU) hours before the temporary 10% Section 122 blanket levy expired — **10-12.5% under a Section 301 forced-labour finding;** **China to a 12.5% added rate (~35%+ effective);** Canada/Mexico/India/Indonesia/UK at 10%. USTR Jamieson Greer framed it as correcting "both a human rights abuse and distortive trade practice." A separate **Section 301 excess-industrial-capacity probe (16 economies)** stays open. The broader **Trump-Xi truce otherwise holds** toward ~November 2026; **Taiwan unchanged** at ~10% + Section 232 metals, no military escalation. *Firms up rates within a holding truce rather than rupturing it — the US-China theatre stays untested for the corpus's decisive-rupture forecast.* (SCMP; USTR; tariff trackers, July 24, 2026.)
- **MAY 15-16 UPDATE**: Trump-Xi Beijing summit CONCLUDED Day 2 (Fri May 15) with DIVERGENT readouts. Trump claimed China would buy '200 Boeing jets' + 'fantastic trade deals'; Beijing's official statement contained ZERO mention of specific commercial agreements (no Boeing confirmation), only vague references to opening doors to US businesses. Xi emphasised Taiwan as the 'most important issue in China-US relations,' warning of 'clashes and even conflicts' if mishandled; White House readouts OMITTED Taiwan; Trump declined Taiwan questions. Both claimed progress 'stabilising ties' but 'differences remain'; agreed to a 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' (Al Jazeera, Newsweek, CNN, Euronews, CNBC). See open-questions: trump-xi-summit-iran-readout-divergence-2026
