### North Korea
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 5):** **A sixteenth consecutive day without a DPRK launch, and the peninsula's only movement was Seoul walking backward.** The South Korean government publicly pushed back on reports of an imminent Hormuz deployment, saying a **review of options including military measures remains in progress and no decision has been made**. The options now reported are a **maritime patrol aircraft**, a **logistics support vessel** and a **mine detection and clearance unit** — **not** the **Cheonghae Unit's** 4,400-tonne destroyer ***Wang Geon*** with its ~260 personnel and naval special warfare boarding team. Expansion of the unit's area of operations requires **both a government decision and National Assembly approval**; South Korean outlets had reported a target of dispatch **before year-end** with parliamentary approval possibly sought this month. **The pressure is documented and American:** Trump publicly criticised Seoul last month for what he described as a direct refusal to assist in the Strait, alongside his order **curtailing a large-scale joint US-ROK exercise** — an alliance-management datum in its own right. **This reference's September 4 finding that the deployment was the first new allied military contribution of the war is withdrawn to untested.** Pyongyang's last launch remains the **~ten short-range ballistic missiles of August 20** during US-ROK exercises, the **ninth ballistic launch of 2026**; the *Just Security* Early Edition for September 4 carried **no Korea item at all**. Standing diplomatic datum unchanged: Trump said on **August 18** that **Kim** had responded to his outreach and called the exchange **“very positive”**; no meeting has been announced.
- **CURRENT STATUS (September 4):** **A fifteenth consecutive day without a DPRK launch, and the peninsula's most consequential military decision this cycle was made in Seoul and points at the Persian Gulf.** Pyongyang's last event remains approximately **ten or more short-range ballistic missiles** fired from **Pyongyang** at about **5 p.m. KST on August 20, 2026** — the third ballistic test that month — timed against large-scale **US-ROK exercises** and Chinese Foreign Minister **Wang Yi's** meeting with President **Lee Jae Myung** in Seoul; Japan's defence ministry issued a coast guard alert at 5:08 p.m. **South Korea is reported to be preparing a military deployment to the Strait of Hormuz** in support of freedom of navigation, aiming to dispatch **before the end of the year**. The candidate force is the **Cheonghae Unit** — currently **Cheonghae Unit 48**, built around the **4,400-tonne destroyer *Wang Geon***, which sailed from **Jinhae on May 15, 2026** on a six-month rotation with about **260 personnel** including a **boarding team from the naval special warfare flotilla** and a **Lynx helicopter** element. Its authorised area of operations is presently confined to waters off **Somalia**; extending it requires a **government decision and National Assembly approval**. **It would be the first new allied military contribution to the Hormuz theatre logged in this war, and it is escort and boarding duty, not landing.** South Korea and Japan remain the world's most **Hormuz-dependent major economies**, and a Korean-operated hull, the ***Senegal Prosperity***, was struck off **Khasab on August 31** carrying two million barrels of Saudi crude. **No inter-Korean incident, no NLL event, and no DPRK response to the prospective Korean Gulf deployment.**
- **CURRENT STATUS (August 22):** **The provocation streak ended — a correction to this briefing's prior framing.** North Korea fired a **short-range ballistic missile on August 6**, its first ballistic testing activity since late June, and **launched again on August 12**, the projectile flying **more than 700 kilometres** before falling into the sea — **Pyongyang's eleventh suspected ballistic test of 2026**, timed against announced **US-South Korean military drills**. This ends the **157-day run without a new DPRK provocation** recorded through August 2. Neither launch produced casualties, an inter-Korean incident or a nuclear test. **The production track is the more consequential one:** Kim Jong Un's early-June order at a missile industrial facility for a **2.5-fold increase in ballistic and cruise missile production** stands; the destroyer **Kang Kon** remains on course for **September commissioning** within a programme targeting **twelve Choe Hyon-class destroyers by 2030**, with a **10,000-tonne guided-missile cruiser** under consideration; **July 21 imagery showed renovated facilities at Sohae** ahead of a first military reconnaissance satellite launch since 2024, **which has not occurred**. **RUSSIA TRACK UNCHANGED:** roughly **15,000 DPRK troops committed** with Zelensky stating a further **30,000 are being prepared**, and South Korean and Western intelligence estimating **around 2,000 DPRK troops killed**, mainly in Kursk; Russia's **July 22 abandonment of support for Korean denuclearisation** stands, as does Kim Yo Jong's **"ultimate shield"** formulation. (Al Jazeera, August 12, 2026; The Diplomat, August 2026; AEI Korean Peninsula Update, July 28, 2026; Bloomberg, July 27, 2026.)

### Plaza Accord

## Status Definitions

- **confirmed**: Prediction has clearly come true
- **partially_confirmed**: Core direction correct but details wrong, or only part of the prediction materialized
- **disconfirmed**: Prediction clearly falsified by events
- **untested**: Not yet testable or insufficient time has passed
- **unfalsifiable**: Cannot be tested empirically
- **contested_unresolved**: The claim **cannot be confirmed from open sources**, **cannot be ruled out from open sources**, **and is being publicly asserted by non-fringe actors**. Deliberately narrow. It exists to prevent the **October Surprise failure mode**, in which absence of documentation silently becomes proof of the negative. When assigned, the `status_note` must name (a) the documented facts the claim rests on, (b) who is publicly asserting it, and (c) what open-source evidence would resolve it. Entries are retired to confirmed or disconfirmed as soon as evidence permits; the live register is `open-questions.json`.
